children.translated_text: Having bowed with my head to the two gods, <s>Pitāmaha</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
I shall proclaim the <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>, which was taught by <s>Brahmā</s>.
Once, when the votary had completed his recitation and was surrounded by his own sons,
on a day without Vedic study, they approached <s>Bharata</s>, skilled in <s>nāṭya</s>.
In ancient times the sages, headed by <s>Ātreya</s>, attended upon him,
and those great-souled men, with senses and minds restrained, asked him:
This teaching, properly composed by the Blessed One and equal to the Veda,

children.text: nāṭyavedaṃ kathaṃ brahmannutpannaḥ kasya vā kṛte ||
children.translated_text: how did the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s> arise, O Brahman, and for whose sake?
How many limbs does it have, what is its extent, and what is its performance like?
All this, as it truly is, Blessed One, you should tell us.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā munīnāṃ bharato muniḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of those sages,
the sage <s>Bharata</s> then replied with words concerning the account of the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>:
Having become pure, and with your minds likewise attentive,
listen to the origin of the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>, fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>.
Formerly, O Brahmins, in the Kṛta age, when the Svāyambhuva interval had passed,
and then, in the Tretā age of <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> when it had arrived,
when the practice of vulgar worldly conduct had arisen and the world had come under the sway of desire and greed,
when, deluded by envy, anger, and the rest, the world was mixed with happiness and suffering,
when <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was filled with gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and great serpents,
and was established under the guardians of the world,
the gods headed by great <s>Indra</s>, it is said, spoke to <s>Pitāmaha</s>:
"We desire an object of play that would be both visible and audible.
This Vedic practice is not to be made heard among the Śūdra classes.
Therefore create another Veda, a fifth one, common to all social classes."
Saying to them, "So be it," and dismissing the king of the gods,
the knower of reality entered meditation and remembered the four Vedas.

children.text: neme vedā yataḥ śrāvyāḥ strīśūdrādyāsu jātiṣu
children.translated_text: "Since these Vedas are not to be heard among women, Śūdras, and similar classes,
I shall create another Veda, a fifth one that is to be heard by all,
righteous, profitable, fame-giving, instructive, and concise,
and one that displays all actions of the world yet to come.
Endowed with the meanings of all śāstras and setting all arts in motion,
I shall make a fifth Veda called <s>nāṭya</s>, together with <s>itihāsa</s>."
Having resolved thus, the Blessed One, recollecting all the Vedas,
then made the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>, arising from the limbs of the four Vedas.
He took recitative text from the Ṛgveda and song itself from the Sāmavedas,
acting from the Yajurveda, and rasas likewise from the Atharvaveda.
The <s>Nāṭyaveda</s> was joined with the Vedas and ancillary Vedas by that great-souled one;
thus it was created by the Blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, the knower of all Vedas.
Having produced the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> said to the lord of the gods:

children.text: itihāso mayā sṛṣṭaḥ sa sureṣu niyujyatām ||
children.translated_text: "This <s>itihāsa</s> has been created by me; let it be assigned among the gods.
Those who are skillful, learned, bold, and tireless,

children.text: teṣvayaṃ nāṭyasaṃjño hi vedaḥ saṃkrāmyatāṃ tvayā ||
children.translated_text: to them let this Veda, known as <s>nāṭya</s>, be handed over by you."
Hearing that speech which had been uttered by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>,
with joined palms and bowed down, replied to <s>Pitāmaha</s>:

children.text: grahaṇe dhāraṇe jñāne prayoge cāsya sattama
children.translated_text: "In receiving, retaining, understanding, and performing this, O best of beings,
the gods, Blessed One, are incapable and unfit for the work of <s>nāṭya</s>.
These seers here, knowers of the secret of the Veda and strict in their vows,

children.text: ete 'sya grahaṇe śaktāḥ prayoge dhāraṇe tathā ||
children.translated_text: are able to receive it, and likewise to perform and preserve it."
But having heard <s>Śakra</s>'s words, the lotus-born one spoke to me:
"You, sinless one, together with your hundred sons, shall be its performer."
Having understood that I had been commanded by <s>Pitāmaha</s> in regard to the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>,
I taught it to my sons, and also its performance according to the truth.

children.text: śāṇḍilyaṃ caiva vātsyaṃ ca kohalaṃ dattilaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: There were <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Vātsya</s>, <s>Kohala</s>, and <s>Dattila</s>,
also <s>Jaṭila</s> and <s>Ambaṣṭa</s>, and likewise <s>Taṇḍu</s> and <s>Agniśikha</s>;
<s>Saindhava</s> together with <s>Pulomā</s>, and likewise <s>Śāḍvali</s> and <s>Vipula</s>;
<s>Kapiñjali</s> and <s>Vādira</s>, and likewise <s>Yamadhūmra</s> and <s>Āyaṇa</s>;
<s>Jambudhvaja</s>, <s>Kākajaṅgha</s>, <s>Svarṇaka</s>, and <s>Tāpasa</s>;

children.text: kaidāriṃ śālikarṇaṃ ca dīrghagātraṃ ca śālikam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaidāri</s>, <s>Śālikarṇa</s>, <s>Dīrghagātra</s>, and <s>Śālika</s>;

children.text: kautsaṃ tāṇḍāyaniṃ caiva piṅgalaṃ citrakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kautsa</s>, <s>Tāṇḍāyani</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, and <s>Citraka</s>;
<s>Bandhula</s> and <s>Bhallaka</s>, and <s>Muṣṭhika</s> and <s>Saindhavāyana</s>;

children.text: taitilaṃ bhārgavaṃ caiva śuciṃ bahulameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Taitila</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, and also <s>Bahula</s>;
<s>Abudha</s>, <s>Budhasena</s>, <s>Pāṇḍukarṇa</s>, and <s>Sukerala</s>;

children.text: ṛjukaṃ maṇḍakaṃ caiva śambaraṃ vañjulaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛjuka</s> and <s>Maṇḍaka</s>, and likewise <s>Śambara</s> and <s>Vañjula</s>;

children.text: māgadhaṃ saralaṃ caiva kartāraṃ cogrameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māgadha</s> and <s>Sarala</s>, and <s>Kartāra</s> and fierce <s>Ugra</s>;
<s>Tuṣāra</s> and <s>Pārṣada</s>, <s>Gautama</s> and <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: viśālaṃ śabalaṃ caiva sunāmaṃ meṣameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśāla</s> and <s>Śabala</s>, and <s>Sunāma</s> and <s>Meṣa</s>;

children.text: kāliyaṃ bhramaraṃ caiva tathā pīṭhamukhaṃ munim
children.translated_text: <s>Kāliya</s> and <s>Bhramara</s>, and likewise the sage <s>Pīṭhamukha</s>;
<s>Nakhakuṭṭa</s> and <s>Aśmakuṭṭa</s>, and <s>Ṣaṭpada</s> together with <s>Uttama</s>;
<s>Pāduka</s> and <s>Upānaha</s>, and <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Āṣasvara</s>;
<s>Agnikuṇḍa</s> and <s>Ājyakuṇḍa</s>, and <s>Vitaṇḍya</s> and <s>Tāṇḍya</s>;
<s>Kartarākṣa</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, <s>Kuśala</s>, and <s>Dussaha</s>;
<s>Lāja</s>, <s>Bhayānaka</s>, <s>Bībhatsa</s>, and <s>Vicakṣaṇa</s>;
<s>Puṇḍrākṣa</s> and <s>Puṇḍranāsa</s>, and also <s>Asita</s> and <s>Sita</s>;
<s>Vidyujjihva</s>, <s>Mahājihva</s>, and <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>;

children.text: śyāmāyanaṃ māṭharaṃ ca lohitāṅgaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śyāmāyana</s>, <s>Māṭhara</s>, and likewise <s>Lohitāṅga</s>;
<s>Saṃvartaka</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, <s>Triśikha</s>, and <s>Śikha</s>.
<s>Śaṅkhavarṇamukha</s>, <s>Śaṇḍa</s>, and also <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>,
<s>Śakranemi</s>, <s>Gabhasti</s>, <s>Aṃśumālin</s>, and likewise <s>Śaṭha</s>,

children.text: vidyutaṃ śātajaṅghaṃ ca raudraṃ vīramathāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyut</s>, <s>Śātajaṅgha</s>, <s>Raudra</s>, and also <s>Vīra</s>--
at the command of the Grandfather, and because we desired the good of the world,
I assigned the hundred sons according to the division of the roles,

children.text: yo yasminkarmaṇi yathā yogyastasmin sa yojitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and each one was appointed to the task for which he was suited.

children.text: bhāratīṃ sātvatīṃ caiva vṛttim ārabhaṭīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Relying on the <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Sāttvatī</s>,

children.text: samāśritaḥ prayogastu prayukto vai mayā dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> <s>vṛttis</s> (styles), I made the performance, O twice-born ones.
Then, having approached and bowed, I informed <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then the teacher of the gods said to me, 'Employ the <s>Kaiśikī</s> as well.

children.text: yacca tasyāḥ kṣamaṃ dravyaṃ tad brūhi dvijasattama
children.translated_text: And tell me, best of the twice-born, what material is suitable for it.'
When he had spoken to me in this way, I replied to the lord:
'Blessed lord, let the material that will serve for the use of the <s>Kaiśikī</s> be given.
It is furnished with dance movements and <s>aṅgahāras</s>, and consists of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and action.
I saw it when the blessed <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> was dancing.
The <s>Kaiśikī</s> has delicate costume and arises from the erotic <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: aśakyā puruṣaiḥ sā tu prayoktuṃ strījanādṛte
children.translated_text: But it cannot be performed by men without women.'
Then the greatly radiant lord created <s>apsarases</s> by his mind,
skilled in the ornaments of drama, and gave them to me for performance:
<s>Mañjukeśī</s>, <s>Sukeśī</s>, <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, and <s>Sulocanā</s>,
<s>Saudāminī</s>, <s>Devadattā</s>, <s>Devasenā</s>, and <s>Manoramā</s>,

children.text: sudatīṃ sundarīṃ caiva vidagdhāṃ vipulāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sudatī</s>, <s>Sundarī</s>, <s>Vidagdhā</s>, and likewise <s>Vipulā</s>,

children.text: sumālāṃ saṃtatiṃ caiva sunandāṃ sumukhīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Sumālā</s>, <s>Saṃtati</s>, <s>Sunandā</s>, and likewise <s>Sumukhī</s>,
<s>Māgadhī</s>, <s>Arjunī</s>, <s>Saralā</s>, <s>Keralā</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,

children.text: nandāṃ sapuṣkalāṃ caiva kalamāṃ caiva me dadau
children.translated_text: and he gave me <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Sapuṣkalā</s>, and <s>Kalamā</s> too.
By <s>Svayambhū</s>, <s>Svāti</s> was assigned to the instruments, together with his pupils,
and the <s>Gandharvas</s> beginning with <s>Nārada</s> were appointed to the practice of song.

children.text: evaṃ nāṭyamidaṃ samyagbuddhvā sarvaiḥ sutaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood this <s>nāṭya</s> (drama) properly, together with all my sons,
and accompanied by <s>Svāti</s> and <s>Nārada</s>, I approached the source of the <s>Veda</s> and the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s>, for the sake of performance, with folded hands.

children.text: nāṭyasya grahaṇaṃ prāptaṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇyaham
children.translated_text: 'The taking up of <s>nāṭya</s> has been accomplished; tell me, what should I do?'
Hearing these words, the Grandfather replied:
'A great occasion for performance has now arrived.
This splendid banner-festival of great <s>Indra</s> is taking place.
Here now this <s>Veda</s> called <s>nāṭya</s> should be performed.'
Then, at that banner-festival, where the <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> had been defeated,
in the victory festival of great <s>Indra</s>, crowded with delighted immortals,
first I made a <s>nāndī</s> (benedictory prelude), joined with words of blessing,
varied, made from the <s>Veda</s>, and furnished with eight limbs and sections.
At its end an enactment was composed, showing how the <s>Daityas</s> were conquered by the gods,
made up of clashes and routs, and consisting of cutting, piercing, and battle.
Then the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, satisfied by the performance,
gave all the necessary implements to my sons.

children.text: prītastu prathamaṃ śakro dattavānsvaṃ dhvajaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Pleased first of all, <s>Śakra</s> gave his auspicious banner.

children.text: brahmā kuṭilakaṃ caiva bhṛṅgāraṃ varuṇaḥ śubham
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> gave the <s>kuṭilaka</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> the auspicious <s>bhṛṅgāra</s> vessel.
<s>Sūrya</s> gave the parasol, <s>Śiva</s> success, and <s>Vāyu</s> the fan,

children.text: viṣṇuḥ siṃhāsanaṃ caiva kubero mukuṭaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: while <s>Viṣṇu</s> gave the throne, and <s>Kubera</s> the crown.
The goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> gave audibility to what was to be seen.
The rest--gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Pannagas</s>--
according to the parts desired in that assembly, grounded in many classes and qualities,

children.text: aṃśāṃśair bhāṣitaṃ bhāvān rasān rūpaṃ balaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: gave, each from their own portions, speech, states, <s>rasas</s>, form, and strength,
and those joyful dwellers in heaven gave them to my sons.
When the performance, depicting the destruction of <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>, had thus begun,

children.text: abhavankṣubhitāḥ sarve daityā ye tatra saṃgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the <s>Daityas</s> who had gathered there became disturbed.
They urged on the <s>Vighnas</s> (obstructors), led by <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and said,
'We will not tolerate this <s>nāṭya</s>; come!'
Then the <s>Vighnas</s>, together with those <s>Asuras</s>, resorted to illusion,

children.text: vācaśceṣṭāṃ smṛtiṃ caiva stambhayanti sma nṛtyatām ||
children.translated_text: and they paralyzed the speech, movement, and memory of the dancers.
Seeing such a disruption of the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage director), the king of the gods
said, 'Why is there disorder in the performance?' and entered meditation.
Then he saw the assembly-place surrounded on every side by the <s>Vighnas</s>,
and the <s>sūtradhāra</s>, along with the others, deprived of awareness and made inert.
Rising quickly, <s>Śakra</s> took up the excellent banner,
his body blazing with every jewel and his eyes somewhat widened.
The king of the gods attacked the <s>Vighnas</s> and <s>Asuras</s> who had come onto the stage,
and with that <s>jarjara</s> he made their bodies shattered.

children.text: nihateṣu ca sarveṣu vighneṣu saha dānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: When all the <s>Vighnas</s> had been slain, together with the <s>Dānavas</s>,
all the dwellers in heaven rejoiced and then spoke these words:
'Ah! This divine weapon has been obtained by you,
by which these <s>Dānavas</s> have been made shattered in every limb.
Since by this those <s>Vighnas</s>, together with the <s>Asuras</s>, have been shattered,
therefore by name this will indeed be the <s>Jarjara</s>.
And the remaining violent beings who come for the sake of violence,
when they merely see the <s>Jarjara</s>, will likewise go away.'
'So be it,' <s>Śakra</s> then said to those gods,
'and this <s>Jarjara</s> will become a protector for all.'

children.text: prayoge prastute hyevaṃ sphīte śakramahe punaḥ
children.translated_text: When the performance had thus begun at the splendid festival of <s>Śakra</s>, again

children.text: trāsaṃ saṃjanayanti sma vighnāḥ śeṣāstu nṛtyatām ||
children.translated_text: the remaining <s>vighnas</s> (obstacles) caused terror among those who were dancing.
Seeing the resolve of those <s>Daityas</s>, born from hostile action,
I approached <s>Brahmā</s>, accompanied by all my sons.
"Blessed lord, the <s>vighnas</s> are resolved upon the destruction of this drama;
command properly the rite for its protection, O lord of gods."
Then <s>Brahmā</s> spoke earnestly to <s>Viśvakarman</s>:
"Make a theatre-building complete with the proper characteristics, O great-minded one."
Then, before long, <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
having made a great, auspicious theatre-house complete with every characteristic,
went to <s>Druhiṇa</s> in the assembly and spoke with joined hands:
"The theatre-house is ready, O god; you ought to inspect that very thing."

children.text: tataḥ saha mahendreṇa suraiḥ sarvaiśca setaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, together with <s>Mahendra</s>, all the gods, and the others,
<s>Druhiṇa</s> came quickly to see the theatre pavilion.
After seeing the theatre-house, <s>Brahmā</s> then said to all the gods:
"This theatre pavilion is to be protected by you with shares of your own portions."
Then the Moon was appointed to the protection of the pavilion,
the <s>Lokapālas</s> in the directions, and the <s>Maruts</s> also in the intermediate directions.
<s>Mitra</s> was placed in the backstage ground, and <s>Varuṇa</s> in the space above;
<s>Agni</s> was placed to protect the altar, and all the celestial beings in the stage equipment.
The four <s>varṇas</s> were then assigned to the pillars,
and the <s>Ādityas</s> and <s>Rudras</s> stood in the spaces between the pillars.
The <s>Bhūtas</s> were placed in the supports, and the <s>Apsarases</s> in the halls;
the <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s> were in all the chambers, and the great ocean was on the surface of the earth.

children.text: dvāraśālāniyuktau tu kṛtāntaḥ kāla eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛtānta</s> and <s>Kāla</s> were appointed to the entrance halls,
and two mighty chief <s>Nāgas</s> were established on the door leaves.
The staff of <s>Yama</s> was on the threshold, and above it the trident was set;
both doorkeepers stood there, <s>Niyati</s> and <s>Mṛtyu</s>.
At the side of the stage-platform <s>Mahendra</s> himself stood,
and in the <s>mattavāraṇī</s> (side gallery) was installed lightning, destroyer of the <s>Daityas</s>.
In the pillars of the <s>mattavāraṇī</s>, for protection, were established
the <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and mighty <s>Guhyakas</s>.
In the <s>jarjara</s> (Indra's banner-staff) was deposited the thunderbolt that destroys <s>Daityas</s>;
in its joints were deposited chiefs of the gods, indeed of immeasurable power.
At the head-joint stood <s>Brahmā</s>, and at the second <s>Śaṅkara</s>;

children.text: tṛtīye ca sthito viṣṇuścaturthe skanda eva ca ||
children.translated_text: at the third stood <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and at the fourth <s>Skanda</s>.
At the fifth were the great <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>;
thus the gods were installed in the <s>jarjara</s> for the destruction of obstacles.

children.text: raṅgapīṭhasya madhye tu svayaṃ brahmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: In the middle of the stage-platform <s>Brahmā</s> himself was established;
for the sake of worship, the scattering of flowers is performed in the middle of the stage.
Those who dwell in the underworld, the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, and <s>Pannagas</s>,
were assigned beneath the stage-platform for protection.
<s>Indra</s> protects the hero, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> the heroine;
the <s>oṃkāra</s> (sacred syllable oṃ) protects the jester, and <s>Hara</s> the remaining <s>prakṛtis</s> (character types).
These deities that have been appointed here for protection
will themselves become the presiding deities, he said.
At this moment the Grandfather was addressed by all the gods:

children.text: sāmnā tāvadime vighnāḥ sthāpyantāṃ vacasā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: "Let these obstacles first be settled by you with conciliatory speech.

children.text: pūrvaṃ sāma prayoktavyaṃ dvitīyaṃ dānameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Sāman</s> (conciliation) should be applied first, and <s>dāna</s> (gift) second;
above those comes <s>bheda</s> (division), and then <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment) is applied."

children.text: devānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā vighnānuvāca ha
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the gods, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to the obstacles:
"Why have you arisen for the destruction of drama?"
Hearing <s>Brahmā</s>'s words, <s>Virūpākṣa</s> spoke a reply,
then, together with the <s>Daityas</s> and groups of <s>vighnas</s>, this speech beginning with conciliation:
"This <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>, which was created by the Blessed Lord at the wish of the gods,
is a rejection of us, made by you for the sake of the gods.
Therefore this should not be done in this way by you, O Grandfather of the world;
as the gods are, so too the <s>Daityas</s> have all issued from you."
Hearing the words of the obstacles, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke a reply:

children.text: alaṃ vo manyunā daityā viṣādaṃ tyajatānaghāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Enough of anger from you, <s>Daityas</s>; abandon despondency, sinless ones.
For you and for the gods, distinguishing auspicious and inauspicious,
the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s> has been made by me with regard to the connection of actions and states.
Here there is not exclusively the exaltation of you or of the gods;
drama is the recounting of the states of this entire three-world.
In one place there is <s>dharma</s> (normative order), in one place play, in one place <s>artha</s> (material aim), in one place calm;
in one place laughter, in one place battle, in one place <s>kāma</s> (desire), in one place killing.
It is <s>dharma</s> for those engaged in <s>dharma</s>, and <s>kāma</s> for those devoted to <s>kāma</s>;
it is restraint for the ill-disciplined, and an act of discipline for the disciplined.
It produces boldness in the timid, and energy in those who think themselves heroic;
it is awakening for the ignorant, and learning for the learned as well.
It is sport for lords, and steadiness for one afflicted by sorrow;
it is livelihood for those dependent on gain, and firmness for minds that are agitated.
Endowed with many states, and consisting of many different conditions,
this drama has been made by me as an imitation of the conduct of the world.
It rests on the actions of superior, inferior, and middling people,
and produces beneficial instruction, firmness, play, happiness, and the like."
In the rasas, the bhāvas, and all activities and actions,
<s>nāṭya</s> (dramatic performance) will become in the world a source of instruction in everything.
For those afflicted by suffering, afflicted by fatigue, afflicted by grief, and for ascetics,
this <s>nāṭya</s> will, at the proper time, bring rest.
It will be righteous, fame-giving, life-promoting, beneficial, and increasing intelligence;
this <s>nāṭya</s> will produce instruction for the world.

children.text: na tajjñānaṃ na tacchilpaṃ na sā vidyā na sā kalā
children.translated_text: There is no knowledge, no craft, no science, and no art,

children.text: nāsau yogo na tatkarma nāṭye 'smin yanna dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: no discipline and no action, that is not seen in this <s>nāṭya</s>.
Therefore no anger should be felt here by you toward the immortals;
this <s>nāṭya</s> will be an imitation of the world with its seven continents.
Since this <s>nāṭya</s> that I have made is an imitation,
of gods, asuras, kings, and householders,
and also of <s>brahmarṣis</s>, <s>nāṭya</s> should be understood as displaying events.
This nature of the world, joined with pleasure and pain,
when furnished with <s>abhinaya</s> (enactment) beginning with bodily expression, is called <s>nāṭya</s>.
It is the imaginative arrangement of narratives from the Vedas, sciences, and histories;
this <s>nāṭya</s> will create recreation in the world.
It is the formulation of supplementary meanings from <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and good conduct;
this <s>nāṭya</s> will bring recreation to the world.
At this point <s>Pitāmaha</s> addressed all the gods:
'Today let sacrificial worship be performed properly in the <s>nāṭyamaṇḍapa</s> (theatre hall).
With presentations of <s>bali</s> offerings and oblations, accompanied by mantras and herbs,
with foods to be eaten, solid eatables, and drinks, let the offering be prepared.'
'All of you, when you have gone to the mortal world, will obtain auspicious worship;

children.text: apūjayitvā raṅgaṃ tu naiva prekṣāṃ pravartayet ||
children.translated_text: but one must not begin a performance without first worshipping the stage.

children.text: apūjayitvā raṅgaṃ tu yaḥ prekṣāṃ kalpayiṣyati
children.translated_text: Whoever arranges a performance without worshipping the stage

children.text: niṣphalaṃ tasya tat jñānaṃ tiryagyoniṃ ca yāsyati ||
children.translated_text: will have that knowledge rendered fruitless, and he will go to an animal birth.
For this worship of the deities of the stage is equivalent to a sacrifice;
therefore it must be performed with every effort by those who practice <s>nāṭya</s>.
A dancer or a patron who will not perform the worship,
or will not have others perform it, meets with decline.
But whoever performs the worship according to rule and as prescribed

children.text: sa lapsyate śubhānarthān svargalokaṃ ca yāsyati ||
children.translated_text: will obtain auspicious benefits and go to the heavenly world.'
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Druhiṇa</s>, together with the deities,
urged me in this way: 'Perform the worship of the stage.'
Thus, in the <s>Bhāratīya Nāṭyaśāstra</s>, the first chapter, called 'The Origin of <s>Nāṭya</s>.'
Then, after hearing <s>Bharata</s>'s words, the sages asked:
'Revered sir, we wish to hear about the worship connected with the stage.

children.text: athavā yāḥ kriyāstatra lakṣaṇaṃ yacca pūjanam
children.translated_text: And what rites are there, what is their definition, and what is the worship,
how is that to be performed by future people in the theatre house?
For here the very beginning of the practice of <s>nāṭya</s> is the <s>nāṭyamaṇḍapa</s> itself;
therefore you should first explain its characteristics.'

children.text: teṣāṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā munīnāṃ bharato 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of the sages, <s>Bharata</s> said:
'Listen to the characteristics and the worship of the theatre building.
For divine beings, creation in houses and groves is mental;
but all human states are to be brought about through expressive enactment.
For men, the procedure described by the rules must be carried out carefully.
Now hear how and where a <s>nāṭyamaṇḍapa</s> should be made,

children.text: tasya vāstu ca pūjā ca yathā yojyā prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and how its site and its worship should be carefully arranged.
Here, after considering the auditorium, wise <s>Viśvakarman</s>
devised, according to śāstra, a threefold arrangement.
The hall is oblong, square, and triangular;

children.text: teṣāṃ trīṇi pramāṇāni jyeṣṭhaṃ madhyaṃ tathāvaram ||
children.translated_text: for these there are three measures: large, middle, and small.
Their measure is prescribed with reference to the <s>hasta</s> (cubit) and the <s>daṇḍa</s> (rod):
one hundred and eight, sixty-four, and thirty-two <s>hastas</s>.
The large is one hundred and eight, while the middle is sixty-four;
the small building is likewise held to be thirty-two <s>hastas</s>.

children.text: devānāṃ tu bhavejjyeṣṭhaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ madhyamaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The large should be for the gods, the middle for kings,
and the small is prescribed for the remaining classes of people.
Among all auditoriums, the middle one is remembered as excellent;

children.text: tatra pāṭhyaṃ ca geyaṃ ca sukhaśrāvyataraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: there recitation and song become easier and more pleasant to hear.
For all auditoriums the rule is remembered as threefold
by practitioners: oblong, square, and triangular.

children.text: kanīyastu smṛtaṃ tryasraṃ caturasraṃ tu madhyamam
children.translated_text: The triangular is remembered as the small, and the square as the middle;
the oblong should be known as the large by practitioners of the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>.
And the measure and characteristic that were prescribed by <s>Viśvakarman</s>
for all auditoriums: understand that as well.

children.text: aṇū rajaśca vālaśca likṣā yūkā yavastathā
children.translated_text: <s>aṇu</s> (atom), <s>rajas</s> (dust mote), <s>vāla</s> (hair), <s>likṣā</s> (nit), <s>yūkā</s> (louse), and <s>yava</s> (barleycorn),

children.text: aṅgulaṃ ca tathā hasto daṇḍaścaiva prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>aṅgula</s> (finger-breadth), <s>hasta</s> (cubit), and <s>daṇḍa</s> (rod), are proclaimed.

children.text: aṇavo 'ṣṭau rajaḥ proktaṃ tānyaṣṭau vāla ucyate
children.translated_text: Eight <s>aṇus</s> are called one <s>rajas</s>; eight of those are called one <s>vāla</s>.
Eight <s>vālas</s> make one <s>likṣā</s>, and one <s>yūkā</s> is eight <s>likṣās</s>.
Eight <s>yūkās</s> should be known as one <s>yava</s>, and eight <s>yavas</s> likewise as one <s>aṅgula</s>.
Twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> are said to be one <s>hasta</s>.
A <s>daṇḍa</s> is four <s>hastas</s>, as prescribed by measure;
by this very measure I shall explain their exact determination.'
As for length, the <s>maṇḍapa</s> (theater hall) should be made sixty-four <s>hastas</s> (cubits).
And it should be thirty-two in breadth, for the one that is here for mortals.
Beyond this, the builders should not make a <s>nāṭyamaṇḍapa</s> (playhouse).
For in such a place the dramatic performance would become indistinct in its <s>bhāvas</s> (expressive states).
But in a very extended hall, the recited text must be uttered with a raised voice.
Because it is unable to carry outward, it would fall greatly into faulty pitch.
And whatever expression is located in the face, joined with various glances,
that, because the building is too extensive, would become utterly indistinct.
Therefore, among all theater houses, the medium-sized one is preferred.

children.text: yāvatpāṭhyaṃ ca geyaṃ ca tatra śravyataraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For in it the recited text and the song will be more clearly audible.
For all theater houses, the rule is remembered as threefold.
By practitioners they are the elongated, the square, and also the triangular.

children.text: kanīyastu smṛtaṃ tryasraṃ caturasraṃ tu madhyamam
children.translated_text: The small one is remembered as triangular, while the square is the medium one.
The large should be known as the elongated one by practitioners of the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s>.
For the gods, creation is mental, in houses and in pleasure gardens alike.
But all human states and forms are produced through effort.
Therefore a human being should not compete with states produced by the gods.
I shall now explain the characteristics of a human dwelling.
First the producer should examine the division and character of the ground.
Then, desiring auspiciousness, he should begin the structure according to proper measure.

children.text: samā sthirā tu kaṭhinā kṛṣṇā gaurī ca yā bhavet
children.translated_text: Ground that is level, stable, hard, and either black or white
is the very ground on which the builders should make the theater hall.
First, after performing purification, he should plough it up with a plough.
He should clear away bones, pegs, skulls, grasses, and shrubs.
After purifying the earth, he should then lay down the measurement.

children.text: trīṇyuttarāṇi saumyaṃ ca viśākhāpi ca revatī ||
children.translated_text: The three <s>Uttarā</s> asterisms, <s>Saumya</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and also <s>Revatī</s>
<s>Hasta</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, and <s>Anurādhā</s> are praised for theatrical work.
With the conjunction of the <s>Puṣya</s> asterism, he should stretch out a white measuring cord.

children.text: kārpāsaṃ bālbajaṃ vāpi mauñjaṃ vālkalameva ca
children.translated_text: The cord should be made by the learned from cotton, <s>bālbaja</s> grass, <s>mauñja</s> grass, or bark fiber.

children.text: sūtraṃ budhaistu kartavyaṃ yasya chedo na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: It must be a cord in which no break is found.
If the cord is half cut, the death of the owner is certain.
With a rope cut by a third, anger in the kingdom is prescribed.
If it is broken by a fourth part, the destruction of the producer is declared.
Or if it slips from the hand, some loss will occur.
Therefore the holding of the rope is always desired with care.

children.text: kāryaṃ caiva prayatnena mānaṃ nāṭyagṛhasya tu ||
children.translated_text: And the measurement of the theater house should be carried out with care.
At a favorable <s>muhūrta</s>, with the lunar day and a good <s>karaṇa</s>,
after satisfying the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he should have the auspicious-day formula proclaimed.

children.text: śāntitoyaṃ tato dattvā tataḥ sūtraṃ prasārayet
children.translated_text: Then, after giving water for pacification, he should stretch out the measuring cord.
Having made it sixty-four <s>hastas</s>, he should again divide those into two.

children.text: pṛṣṭhato yo bhavedbhāgo dvidhābhūtasya tasya tu
children.translated_text: As for the part that is at the rear of that divided space,
he should plan the <s>raṅgaśīrṣa</s> (stage-head) with an equal half-division.
Then in the western division he should designate the <s>nepathyagṛha</s> (backstage room).
The parts should be divided according to rule, properly and in due order.
Under an auspicious conjunction of asterisms, the establishment of the <s>maṇḍapa</s>
should take place with the sounds of conches and kettledrums, and with <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, and the like,
while all musical instruments are being sounded; the installation must indeed be done.
Undesirable persons are to be driven away, likewise heretics and sectarian ascetics;
also those wearing ochre robes and persons who are physically impaired.
At night a <s>bali</s> (offering) should be made, furnished with various foods,
endowed with perfumes, flowers, and fruits, and addressed to the ten directions.
To the east it should have white rice, and to the south dark-blue rice.
To the west the offering is yellow, and to the north it is red.

children.text: yādṛśaṃ diśi yasyāṃ tu daivataṃ parikalpitam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever deity has been assigned to whichever direction,
an offering of that same kind should be given there, preceded by mantra.
At the installation, ghee-rice pudding should be given to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Likewise <s>madhuparka</s> should be given to the king, and molasses rice to the builders.

children.text: nakṣatreṇa tu kartavyaṃ mūlena sthāpanaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The installation should be performed by the learned under the <s>Mūla</s> asterism.
At a favorable <s>muhūrta</s>, with the lunar day and a good <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ tu sthāpanaṃ kṛtvā bhittikarma prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the installation in this way, he should set the wall-work in motion.
When the wall-work is completed, then comes the installation of the pillars.
It should be done with an auspicious lunar day, asterismal conjunction, and <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: stambhānāṃ sthāpanaṃ kāryaṃ rohiṇyā śravaṇena vā
children.translated_text: The installation of the pillars should be performed under <s>Rohiṇī</s> or <s>Śravaṇa</s>.
by a well-qualified teacher who has fasted for three nights.

children.text: stambhānāṃ sthāpanaṃ kāryaṃ prāpte sūryodaye śubhe
children.translated_text: The installation of the pillars should be done when an auspicious sunrise has arrived.
At the first, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> pillar, the rite is prepared with ghee and mustard.
The entire rite should be white, and he should give rice pudding.
Then at the <s>kṣatriya</s> pillar, cloth, garlands, and unguents
should all be given in red, and molasses rice should be given to the twice-born.
At the <s>vaiśya</s> pillar, the rite should be performed in the northwestern quarter.
Everything yellow should be given, and ghee-rice should be given to the twice-born.
At the <s>śūdra</s> pillar, the rite should be performed properly, taking its place in the northeastern part.
With blue predominating, <s>kṛsara</s> (a rice-and-bean dish) is the food for the twice-born.
At the previously mentioned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> pillar, with white garlands and unguents,
he should deposit gold at the base, in the form of an ear ornament.
And copper should be placed below in the pillar designated <s>kṣatriya</s>.
At the base of the <s>Vaiśya</s>-pillar he should deposit silver,
and at the base of the <s>Śūdra</s>-pillar he should place iron as well.
Gold, however, is to be deposited at the bases of all the pillars,
with cries of auspiciousness, proclamation of a holy day, and shouts of victory.
The setting up of the pillars should be performed, preceded by flower garlands,
with gifts of jewels, gifts of cows, and abundant gifts of garments.
After satisfying the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he should then raise the pillars.
A pillar must be immovable, unshaken, and likewise not bent.
For in the proper raising of a pillar these are declared to be the faults:
if it moves, drought is said to result; if it bends, there is fear of death;
if it shakes, terrible fear arises from an enemy army.
Therefore he should raise an auspicious pillar free from these faults.

children.text: pavitre brāhmaṇastambhe dātavyā dakṣiṇā ca gauḥ
children.translated_text: At the consecrated <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-pillar the fee to be given is a cow.
For the remaining pillars, at the installation, food is to be prepared according to the patron.
That gift, purified by mantra, should be given by the wise teacher of drama.
He should feed the priest and the king with honeyed milk-rice,
and likewise all the workers with <s>kṛsarā</s> (rice-and-pulse gruel) rich in salt.
After carrying out this whole rite, while every musical instrument is being played,
the pure man, having consecrated the pillars according to rule, should raise them.
As the mountain <s>Meru</s> is immovable, and mighty <s>Himavat</s> too,
so may you be immovable, bringing victory to the king.

children.text: stambhadvāraṃ ca bhittiṃ ca nepathyagṛhameva ca ||
children.translated_text: The pillars, the door, the wall, and the tiring-house also
should be raised in this way by one who knows, through the rite prescribed by rule.
At the side of the <s>raṅgapīṭha</s> (stage-platform), the <s>mattavāraṇī</s> (side gallery) should be made,
furnished with four pillars and proportioned to the stage-platform.
The <s>mattavāraṇī</s> should be made with an elevation of one and a half hastas,
and the theatre hall should be made equal to those two in height.

children.text: tasyāṃ mālyaṃ ca dhūpaṃ ca gandhaṃ vastraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: In it, garlands, incense, perfume, and cloth as well,
things of various colors are to be given, and a <s>bali</s> (offering) dear to the spirits.
Milk-rice should be offered there below the pillars by skilled men.
At the feeding, <s>kṛsarā</s> dishes too are to be given, and food for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
Thus, with ritual preliminaries, the <s>mattavāraṇī</s> should be made.
Then the <s>raṅgapīṭha</s> should be made by the rite prescribed by rule.
The <s>raṅgaśīrṣa</s> (stage-head) should be made furnished with six timbers.
Here two doors should be made for the tiring-house.

children.text: pūraṇe mṛttikā cātra kṛṣṇā deyā prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the filling there, black earth should be carefully supplied.
It should be ploughed up with a plough, free from clods, grass, and gravel.

children.text: lāṅgale śuddhavarṇau tu dhuryau yojyau prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two pure-colored draught animals should be carefully yoked to the plough.
The workers here should be men who are free from defects of limb,
and the earth should be carried by people with complete limbs in new baskets.
In this manner the <s>raṅgaśīrṣa</s> should be carefully prepared.

children.text: kūrmapṛṣṭhaṃ na kartavyaṃ matsyapṛṣṭhaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: It should not be made like a tortoise's back, nor likewise like a fish's back.
A <s>raṅgaśīrṣa</s> shaped like the surface of a clean mirror is praised.

children.text: ratnāni cātra deyāni pūrve vajraṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Jewels should be placed here by experts: a diamond in the east,

children.text: vaiḍūryaṃ dakṣiṇe pārśve sphaṭikaṃ paścime tathā
children.translated_text: <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) on the southern side, and crystal in the west,

children.text: pravālamuttare caiva madhye tu kanakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: coral in the north, and gold in the middle.
Having made the stage-head in this way, he should undertake the woodwork.
It should have projections and counter-projections and employ varied craftsmanship;
it should be furnished with various joinings and adorned with many <s>vyālas</s> (mythic beasts);
it should be decorated all around with <s>śālabhañjikās</s> as well;
it should have projecting niches and recesses, with platforms variously interlaced;
it should have varied arrangements and ornamental lattice windows;
it should be provided with good bases and supports and filled with rows of <s>kapota</s> mouldings;
and it should be beautified with pillars arranged on various paved surfaces.
After carrying out the rule for woodwork in this way, he should undertake the wall-work.

children.text: stambhaṃ vā nāgadantaṃ vā vātāyanamathāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: He should not make a door open onto a pillar, a <s>nāgadanta</s> bracket, or a window,

children.text: koṇaṃ vā sapratidvāraṃ dvāraviddhaṃ na kārayet
children.translated_text: nor onto a corner or an opposite doorway, so that it is struck by a door.
The <s>nāṭyamaṇḍapa</s> (theatre hall) should have the form of a mountain cave and two levels,
with small windows, free from wind, and carrying a deep sound.
Therefore the theatre hall should be made windless by the builders,
so that the sound of the <s>kutapa</s> (musical ensemble) will be deep.
After completing the rule for wall-work, he should have plaster applied to the walls.
Its exterior whitewashing should be carried out carefully.
Then, when the walls have been plastered and smoothed everywhere,
and have become even and beautiful, he should undertake the painting.
In the painting, men and women should be depicted,
and creeper-patterns should be made, along with scenes of conduct and enjoyment.
In this way the <s>vikṛṣṭa</s> (oblong) theatre building should be made by the producers.
Now again I shall state the characteristics of the <s>caturaśra</s> (square) one.
It should be made thirty-two hastas on every side,
a theatre hall set on a well-divided auspicious ground by those who know drama.

children.text: yo vidhiḥ pūrvamuktastu lakṣaṇaṃ maṅgalāni ca ||
children.translated_text: The procedure, the characteristics, and the auspicious rites that were stated before:
all those, without remainder, should be performed for the square one also, as for the oblong.

children.text: caturaśraṃ samaṃ kṛtvā sūtreṇa pravibhajya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having made the square even and divided it with a cord,

children.text: bāhyataḥ sarvataḥ kāryā bhittiḥ śliṣṭeṣṭakā dṛḍhā
children.translated_text: an outer wall should be made on every side, firm with closely joined bricks.
There, on the inside, those standing above the stage-platform are to be made.
Ten pillars, fit for supporting the pavilion, should be set up by the practitioners.
And outside the pillars there should also be a little platform shaped like steps.
The seating arrangement for the spectators should be made with bricks and wood,
with elevations measured by <s>hastas</s> (cubits), raised up from sections of the ground.
One should arrange the rule for seating so that the stage-platform can be seen.
And after another six, again pillars should be placed according to the directions.
The expert should establish them by rule, firm for supporting the pavilion.
And again he should arrange eight pillars above them.
Then a platform should be established with a measure of eight <s>hastas</s>.

children.text: viddhāsyamaṣṭahastaṃ ca pīṭhaṃ teṣu tato nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having made the platform eight <s>hastas</s>, he should then set it upon them.
There pillars should be supplied by experts for supporting the pavilion.
These supports of the bearing structure should be adorned with <s>śālastrī</s> figures.
Then the backstage house should be made carefully.
There should be one door there, an entrance to the stage-platform.
And another, for the entrance of the people, should be made facing it.
The second door should indeed be made facing the stage.
The stage-platform should be made eight <s>hastas</s> in measure,
square, level, and adorned with a <s>vedikā</s> (railing or terrace).
The <s>mattavāraṇī</s>, specified by the earlier measurement, should be made,
furnished with four pillars at the side of the <s>vedikā</s>.

children.text: samunnataṃ samaṃ caiva raṅgaśīrṣaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: The stage-head should be made raised and even.

children.text: vikṛṣṭe tūnnataṃ kāryaṃ caturaśre samaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: In an oblong house it should be raised, and in a square one likewise level.
Thus, by this rule, the square house is completed.
After this I shall explain the characteristics of a triangular house.
A triangular, three-cornered theatre house should be made by the practitioners.
In its middle one should make the stage-platform triangular as well.

children.text: dvāraṃ tenaiva koṇena kartavyaṃ tasya veśmanaḥ
children.translated_text: A door of that building should be made at that very corner,
and a second one should be made behind the stage-platform.
The rule that applies to the square house, concerning walls and pillars,
all of that is to be applied by practitioners to the triangular house also.
Thus, by this rule, theatre houses should be made by the wise.
Now again I shall explain their worship in due order.
When the auspicious theatre house has been made, complete with all its characteristics,
cows should dwell there for seven days together with twice-born men devoted to recitation.
Then he should perform the <s>adhivāsa</s> (preliminary consecration) of the building and likewise of the stage-platform.
At the coming of night, his body should be sprinkled with water purified by mantra.
Having gone to the proper assigned place, initiated, restrained, and pure,
having fasted for three nights, the <s>nāṭyācārya</s> (drama teacher), wearing new garments,
should bow to <s>Mahādeva</s>, to <s>Bhava</s>, the origin of all worlds,
and to <s>Jagatpitāmaha</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and also <s>Guha</s>,

children.text: sarasvatīṃ ca lakṣmīṃ ca siddhiṃ medhāṃ dhṛtiṃ smṛtim
children.translated_text: to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Siddhi</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, and <s>Smṛti</s>,
to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, the world-protectors, and the two <s>Aśvins</s>,
to <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the gods, the classes, the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, and also <s>Kali</s>,

children.text: mṛtyuṃ ca niyatiṃ caiva kāladaṇḍaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Mṛtyu</s>, <s>Niyati</s>, and also the staff of <s>Kāla</s>,
to the weapon of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and to <s>Vāsuki</s>, king of serpents,
to the thunderbolt, lightning, and the oceans, to the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, and sages,
to the <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, and great lords,
to the <s>Asuras</s>, the obstacles to <s>nāṭya</s>, and also other <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
and likewise to the <s>Nāṭyakumārīs</s> and to <s>Mahāgrāmaṇī</s>,
to the <s>Yakṣas</s>, the <s>Guhyakas</s>, and the hosts of beings as well.
Having bowed with joined palms to these and to other gods and seers,
and having summoned them to their respective places, he should then say:
'By you our protection must be undertaken during the night,
and help must be given in this <s>nāṭya</s>, together with your retinues.'
Having worshipped all of them in one place and set the <s>kutapa</s> (musical ensemble) in action,
he should perform worship for the <s>Jarjara</s> staff, for the success of <s>nāṭya</s>:
'You are the weapon of great <s>Indra</s>, the destroyer of all <s>Dānavas</s>,
made by all the gods and the remover of every obstacle.

children.text: nṛpasya vijayaṃ śaṃsa ripūṇāṃ ca parājayam
children.translated_text: Proclaim the king's victory and the defeat of his enemies,
the welfare of cows and brahmins, and the increase of <s>nāṭya</s>.'
Having done this according to rule and remained in the theatre pavilion,
when the night has passed into dawn, he should begin the worship here.

children.text: ārdrāyāṃ vā maghāyāṃ vā yāmye pūrveṣu vā triṣu
children.translated_text: In <s>Ārdrā</s> or <s>Maghā</s>, or in <s>Yāmya</s>, or in the three <s>Pūrvās</s>,
or in <s>Āśleṣā</s> or <s>Mūla</s>, the worship of the stage should be performed.

children.text: ācāryeṇa tu yuktena śucinā dīkṣitena ca
children.translated_text: By a properly prepared, pure, and initiated teacher,
the illumination of the stage and the worship of the deities should be performed.
At the end of the day, in a fierce and dreadful <s>muhūrta</s> belonging to <s>Yama</s>,

children.text: ācamya tu yathānyāyaṃ devatā vai niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: after sipping water according to rule, he should install the deities.
There should be red protective bands, thread, and red perfumes, ritually honored,

children.text: raktāḥ sumanasaścaiva yacca raktaṃ phalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: red flowers, and whatever fruit may be red.
With barley, white mustard seed, parched grain, unbroken rice, and rice grains,
with powder of <s>nāgapuṣpa</s>, husked grains, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
with these substances he should perform the installation of the deities.
First he should draw a <s>maṇḍala</s> according to place and according to rule.
The <s>maṇḍala</s> should be made sixteen <s>hastas</s> on every side,
and in it he should make doors in the four directions according to the prescribed rule.

children.text: madhye caivātra kartavye dve rekhe tiryagūrdhvage
children.translated_text: And here in the middle two lines should be made, one running across and one upward.
By the division of their compartments one should place the deities there.
In its center one should place <s>Brahmā</s>, seated on a lotus.
First the blessed <s>Śiva</s> should be placed together with the hosts of beings.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, and the Moon,

children.text: sarasvatī ca lakṣmīśca śraddhā medhā ca pūrvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Śraddhā</s>, and <s>Medhā</s> should be placed to the east.
To the southeast <s>Vahni</s> should be placed together with <s>Svāhā</s>,
as well as the <s>Viśvedevāḥ</s>, with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the serpent hosts.
To the south <s>Yama</s> and <s>Mitra</s>, each with his attendants, should be placed.
One should also place the <s>Pitṛs</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Uragas</s>, and <s>Guhyakas</s>.
In the southwest one should place the <s>Rākṣasas</s> and the beings.
In the west one should place the oceans and <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of aquatic creatures.
Likewise, in the northwestern direction one should place the seven winds.
There too <s>Garuḍa</s> should be installed together with the birds.
In the northern direction one should likewise place <s>Dhanada</s>.
And there one should place the Mothers of <s>nāṭya</s>, as well as the <s>Yakṣas</s> with the <s>Guhyakas</s>.
Likewise in the northeast, one should place <s>Nandī</s> and the other lords of hosts,
and the <s>Brahmarṣis</s> and hosts of beings, each according to its proper share.

children.text: stambhe sanatkumāraṃ tu dakṣiṇe dakṣameva ca
children.translated_text: On the southern pillar one should place <s>Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Dakṣa</s>,
and on the northern pillar <s>Grāmaṇī</s> should be installed for worship.
By this very procedure, in the proper place and according to rule,
one should install all the deities so that they are well pleased.

children.text: sthāne sthāne yathānyāyaṃ viniveśya tu devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed the deities in each place according to what is proper,

children.text: tāsāṃ prakurvīta tataḥ pūjanaṃ tu yathārhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should then perform their worship as each deserves.
White garlands and unguents are to be given to the deities,
and red garlands and unguents to the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, and <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: gandhaṃ mālyaṃ ca dhūpaṃ ca yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: After giving fragrance, garland, and incense properly and in order,

children.text: dattvā tataḥ prakurvīta baliṃ pūjāṃ yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: one should then perform the <s>bali</s> (offering) and worship according to rule.
One should worship <s>Brahmā</s> with <s>madhuparka</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> with milk-rice pudding.
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, and the others are then to be worshipped with sweet cakes.
<s>Hutabhuk</s> is to be worshipped with ghee-rice, while <s>Soma</s> and <s>Arka</s> are to be worshipped with jaggery-rice.
The <s>Viśvedevāḥ</s> together with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and the sages, are to be worshipped with honeyed milk-rice.
<s>Yama</s> and <s>Mitra</s> should be worshipped with <s>apūpa</s> cakes and sweet cakes.
One should satisfy the <s>Pitṛs</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and <s>Uragas</s> with ghee and milk.
With cooked food, meat, liquor, <s>sīdhu</s>, and fruit-wines,
one should worship the hosts of beings, and with chickpeas mixed with <s>palala</s> paste.
By this same procedure the <s>mattavāraṇī</s> should be fully worshipped.

children.text: pakvānnena tu māṃsena saṃpūjyā rakṣasāṃ gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The groups of <s>Rākṣasas</s> should be worshipped with cooked food and meat.
One should honor the <s>Dānavas</s> with gifts of liquor and meat.
The expert should worship the remaining groups of gods with rice dishes accompanied by <s>apūpa</s> cakes and <s>utkārikā</s> cakes.
With fish and flour-made foods one should worship the oceans and the rivers as well.
After worshipping <s>Varuṇa</s> too, ghee and milk-rice pudding should be given.
One should also worship the sages with various roots and fruits,
and the winds and birds with varied foods and prepared dishes.

children.text: mātṝr nāṭyasya sarvāstā dhanadaṃ ca sahānugaiḥ
children.translated_text: All those Mothers of <s>nāṭya</s>, and <s>Dhanada</s> with his attendants,
should be worshipped with <s>apūpa</s> cakes mixed with <s>lopikā</s>, and with foods to be chewed and eaten.
Thus for these beings the <s>bali</s> should be made, consisting of many kinds of food.
Next the rite of <s>bali</s> will be stated according to the rule of mantras.
O god of gods, greatly blessed grandsire of all worlds,
accept from me this entire <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra.
O god of gods, greatly blessed <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>,
O god, may the <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra and presented by me, be accepted.
O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> of immeasurable course, lotus-naveled one, best of gods,
O god, may the <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra and offered by me, be accepted.
O <s>Purandara</s>, lord of the immortals, wielder of the thunderbolt, <s>Śatakratu</s>,
O god, may the <s>bali</s>, preceded by rule and mantra, be accepted.
O <s>Skanda</s>, commander of the divine army, blessed one dear to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
O six-faced one, may the <s>bali</s> be accepted with a pleased mind.
O <s>Mahādeva</s>, great yogin, god of gods, best of gods,
O god, accept the <s>bali</s> and protect us from obstruction that ever arises.
O goddess, greatly blessed among gods, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, beloved of <s>Hari</s>,
O Mother, may the <s>bali</s> offered by me with devotion be accepted.
All you descendants of <s>Pulastya</s>, born from many causes,
great mighty lords of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, accept my <s>bali</s>.
May <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Siddhi</s>, <s>Mati</s>, and <s>Medhā</s>, honored by all worlds,
O goddesses, accept from me this <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra.
O <s>Māruta</s>, knower of the powers of all beings, life of the world,
O god, may the <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra and presented by me, be accepted.
O <s>Hutāśana</s>, mouth of the gods, best of gods, smoke-bannered one,

children.text: bhaktyā samudyato deva baliḥ samprati gṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: O god, may the <s>bali</s> now prepared with devotion be accepted.
O <s>Divākara</s>, foremost of all planets, mass of radiance,

children.text: bhaktyā mayodyato deva baliḥ samprati gṛhyatām ||
children.translated_text: O god, may the <s>bali</s> now prepared by me with devotion be accepted.
O <s>Soma</s>, lord of all planets, king of twice-born ones, beloved of the world,
may this <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra and presented by me, be accepted.
All you great lords of hosts, with <s>Nandīśvara</s> at your head,
may the <s>bali</s> now offered by me with devotion be accepted.
Homage to all the <s>Pitṛs</s>; may they accept this <s>bali</s>.

children.text: bhūtebhyaśca namo nityaṃ yeṣāmeṣa baliḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: And constant homage to the beings for whom this <s>bali</s> is dear.

children.text: kāmapāla namo nityaṃ yasyāyaṃ te vidhiḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāmapāla</s>, constant homage to you; this procedure has been made for you.
May <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Tumburu</s>, together with all the <s>Gandharvas</s> headed by <s>Viśvāvasu</s>,
all accept my prepared <s>bali</s> (offering).
May <s>Yama</s> and blessed <s>Mitra</s>, the two lords worshipped by the world,
accept this <s>bali</s> of mine, preceded by mantra.
Again and again homage to the serpents who have gone to <s>Rasātala</s>;
worshipped, destroyers of sin, may they grant success to the <s>nāṭya</s>.
The god <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of all waters, whose vehicle is a goose,
may he be worshipped and pleased, together with oceans, rivers, and streams.
O <s>Vainateya</s>, great being, lord of all birds, mighty one,
O god, may the <s>bali</s>, purified by mantra and prepared by me, be accepted.
May the overseer of wealth, lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, world-protector, lord of riches,
together with the <s>Guhyakas</s> and <s>Yakṣas</s>, accept my <s>bali</s>.
Homage to the Mothers of <s>nāṭya</s>, beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s>; homage, homage.
With gracious and pleased faces, may the <s>bali</s> be accepted today.
May all the weapons of <s>Rudra</s> accept my <s>bali</s>,
and also the weapons of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, prepared by me with devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Likewise may <s>Kṛtānta</s> and <s>Kāla</s>, the two lords over the death of all living beings,
and <s>Mṛtyu</s> and <s>Niyati</s> accept my <s>bali</s>.
And whatever guardian deities of the site dwell in this <s>mattavāraṇī</s> (side platform),
may they properly accept this <s>bali</s> of mine, purified by mantra.

children.text: anye ye devagandharvā diśo daśa samāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever other gods and <s>Gandharvas</s> inhabit the ten directions,
whether celestial, atmospheric, or earthly, for them too this <s>bali</s> has been made.
He should set down a jar filled with water, accompanied by a garland of flowers,
in the middle of the stage, and he should have gold placed there.

children.text: ātodyāni tu sarvāṇi kṛtvā vastrottarāṇi tu
children.translated_text: Having covered all the musical instruments with cloths,
he should worship them with perfumes, garlands, incense, foods to chew, and foods to eat.
After worshipping all the deities in due order,
the <s>jarjara</s> should then be specially worshipped as the crusher of obstacles.

children.text: śvetaṃ śirasi vastraṃ syānnīlaṃ raudre ca parvaṇi
children.translated_text: A white cloth should be on its head, and a blue one on the <s>parvan</s> (joint) of <s>Rudra</s>;

children.text: viṣṇuparvaṇi vai pītaṃ raktaṃ skandasya parvaṇi ||
children.translated_text: on the <s>parvan</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s> there should be yellow, and on the <s>parvan</s> of <s>Skanda</s> red.

children.text: mṛḍaparvaṇi citraṃ tu deyaṃ vastraṃ hitārthinā
children.translated_text: On the <s>parvan</s> of <s>Mṛḍa</s>, a variegated cloth should be given by one seeking welfare;
matching incense, garlands, and unguent should also be offered.
He should wrap all the musical instruments with cloths,
and worship them with perfumes, garlands, incense, foods to chew, and foods to eat.
After carrying out the whole procedure in this way, with perfumes, garlands, and unguents,
he should consecrate the <s>jarjara</s> with mantra for the crushing of obstacles.
For the destruction of obstacles here, by the gods headed by <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
you were fashioned, mighty in power, with the essence of the thunderbolt and a great body.
May <s>Brahmā</s>, together with all the hosts of gods, protect your head;

children.text: dvitīyaṃ ca haraḥ parva tṛtīyaṃ ca janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hara</s> protect the second <s>parvan</s>, and <s>Janārdana</s> the third.
May <s>Kumāra</s> protect your fourth, and the best of serpents the fifth;

children.text: nityaṃ sarve 'pi pāntu tvāṃ surārthe ca śivo bhava ||
children.translated_text: may all of them always guard you, and be auspicious for the gods' purpose.
For you were born under the <s>Abhijit</s> constellation, O destroyer of foes;
bring victory and prosperity to the king.

children.text: jarjaraṃ pūjayitvaivaṃ baliṃ sarvaṃ nivedya ca
children.translated_text: After worshipping the <s>jarjara</s> in this way and presenting the whole <s>bali</s>,
he should then perform an oblation in the fire, preceded by mantra-offerings.
From the blazing fire itself, with flaming torches, he should perform the purifying sweep,
and bring about an increase of radiance for the king and for the dancing women.
Having illuminated the king and the dancing women while the instruments sound,
and sprinkling them again with water purified by mantra, he should say to them:
'You are born in a great family and are adorned with a mass of virtues;

children.text: yadvo janma guṇopetaṃ tadvo bhavatu nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that birth of yours, endowed with virtues, remain yours always.'
Having spoken this statement, the wise man, for the prosperity of the king,
should apply blessings for the successful accomplishment of the practice of <s>nāṭya</s>.
May <s>Sarasvatī</s>, steadfastness, intelligence, modesty, fortune, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, memory, and thought,

children.text: pāntu vo mātaraḥ saumyāḥ siddhidāśca bhavantu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gentle Mothers, protect you and become grantors of success for you.
Having performed the <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) according to rule, with the oblation preceded by mantra,
the <s>nāṭyācārya</s> (theatre teacher) should then carefully break the jar.

children.text: abhinne tu bhavetkumbhe svāminaḥ śatruto bhayam
children.translated_text: If the jar remains unbroken, there will be danger from enemies for the patron;

children.text: bhinne caiva tu vijñeyaḥ svāminaḥ śatrusaṃkṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but if it is broken, the destruction of the patron's enemies should be understood.
When the jar has been broken, the <s>nāṭyācārya</s> should then carefully

children.text: pragṛhya dīpikāṃ dīptāṃ sarvaṃ raṅgaṃ pradīpayet ||
children.translated_text: take up a blazing lamp and illuminate the whole stage.
With shouts, claps, leaps, and rushes,

children.text: raṅgamadhye tu tāṃ dīptāṃ saśabdāṃ saṃprayojayet ||
children.translated_text: he should set that blazing, noisy lamp in motion in the middle of the stage.
With the roars of conches and kettledrums, and likewise with <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> and <s>paṇavas</s>,
with all the instruments resounding, he should make battles take place on the stage.

children.text: tatra chinnaṃ ca bhinnaṃ ca dāritaṃ ca saśoṇitam
children.translated_text: There, anything cut, broken, torn open, bloody,
wounded, blazing, or strained is an omen, a sign of success.
A stage properly worshipped indeed brings good fortune to the patron,
to the city, including children and elders, and likewise to the countryside.
But a stage badly worshipped, badly occupied by the deities,
causes the destruction of the <s>nāṭya</s> and also misfortune for the king.
Whoever, abandoning this procedure, carries things out as he pleases,
quickly meets with decline and goes to an animal birth.
For this worship of the deities of the stage is equal to a sacrifice.

children.text: apūjayitvā raṅgaṃ tu naiva prekṣāṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Without worshiping the stage, one should by no means put on a spectacle.
When worshiped, these deities worship in return; when honored, they honor in return.
Therefore <s>raṅgapūjana</s> (stage worship) must be performed with every effort.
Fire, fanned by the wind, does not burn so fiercely
as an improper performance, once put on, burns at once.
By a <s>nāṭyācārya</s> (teacher of drama) who knows the treatise, is disciplined, pure, and consecrated,
and is calm, the <s>raṅgapūjana</s> (stage worship) should be performed.
But he who, with an agitated mind, gives the <s>bali</s> (offering) in the wrong place

children.text: mantrahīno yathā hotā prāyaścittī bhavettu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes liable to <s>prāyaścitta</s> (atonement), like a <s>hotṛ</s> priest without mantras.
Thus this rule that has been prescribed for worshiping the deities of the stage

children.text: nave nāṭyagṛhe kāryaḥ prekṣāyāṃ ca prayoktṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be performed by producers in a new theater house and also at a spectacle.

children.text: evaṃ tu pūjanaṃ kṛtvā mayā proktaḥ pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Having performed the worship in this way, I addressed <s>Pitāmaha</s>:

children.text: ājñāpaya prabho kṣipraṃ kaḥ prayogaḥ prayujyatām ||
children.translated_text: 'Command me quickly, lord: what performance is to be put on?'
Then I was told by <s>Bhagavat</s>, 'Stage the <s>Amṛtamanthana</s> (Churning of Nectar).
This arouses energy and also brings delight to the gods.
This <s>samavakāra</s> (dramatic form), which accomplishes <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth,
was composed earlier by me, learned one; let that performance be staged.'
When that <s>samavakāra</s> was performed, the gods and <s>Dānavas</s>
all became delighted on seeing the actions and emotional states represented.
Then, after some time, <s>Ambujasambhava</s> said to me:
'Today let us show drama to the great-souled <s>Trinetra</s>.'
Then, going together with the gods to the abode of the Bull-emblemed one,
and after worshiping <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s> spoke these words:
'O best of gods, this <s>samavakāra</s> that has been created by me,
you should graciously favor by hearing and seeing it.'
'Let us see it,' the lord of the gods said to <s>Druhiṇa</s>.

children.text: tato māmāha bhagavān sajjo bhava mahāmate ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavat</s> said to me, 'Be ready, great-minded one.'
Then on a slope of <s>Himavat</s>, crowded with many serpents,
thronged with many hosts of <s>bhūtas</s>, and rich in beautiful caves and waterfalls,
the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s> (preliminary stage rite) was first performed there, O best of the twice-born,
and the <s>Tripuradāha</s> (Burning of Tripura), called a <s>ḍima</s>, was also staged.
Then the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> were delighted by the recounting of actions and states,
and <s>Mahādeva</s>, greatly pleased, then said to <s>Pitāmaha</s>:

children.text: aho nāṭyamidaṃ samyak tvayā sṛṣṭaṃ mahāmate
children.translated_text: 'Ah, this drama has been well created by you, great-minded one;

children.text: yaśasyaṃ ca śubhārthaṃ ca puṇyaṃ buddhivivardhanam ||
children.translated_text: it brings fame, auspicious benefit, merit, and the increase of understanding.
I too have conceived this dance while dancing at the twilight times,
adorned with <s>aṅgahāras</s> (dance sequences) joined with various <s>karaṇas</s> (dance units).
Let it be properly employed by you in this rule of the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s>,
in the applications of the <s>vardhamānaka</s>, in songs, and in <s>āsāritas</s>.
And in the <s>mahāgītas</s> you will represent the meanings quite properly.
And this <s>pūrvaraṅga</s> which was performed by you in pure form,
when mixed with these, will be called <s>citra</s> (variegated).'
After hearing the words of <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> replied:
'Explain the use of the <s>aṅgahāras</s>, O best of the gods.'
Then <s>Bhuvaneśvara</s>, summoning <s>Taṇḍu</s>, said:
'Explain the use of the <s>aṅgahāras</s> to <s>Bharata</s>.'
Then the <s>aṅgahāras</s> that were taught by the great-souled <s>Taṇḍu</s>,
I shall explain to you, joined with <s>karaṇas</s> and accompanied by <s>recakas</s>.
The <s>aṅgahāras</s> are known as <s>Sthirahasta</s> and also <s>Paryastaka</s>,
as <s>Sūcividdha</s> and likewise <s>Apaviddha</s>,
then <s>Ākṣiptaka</s> is to be known, and <s>Udghaṭṭita</s> is remembered,
and <s>Viṣkambha</s> is taught, as also <s>Aparājita</s>,
and <s>Viṣkambhāpasṛta</s>, as well as <s>Mattākrīḍa</s>,
and <s>Svastika</s>, <s>Recita</s>, and <s>Pārśvasvastika</s>,
<s>Vṛścikāpasṛta</s> is stated, and another is <s>Bhramara</s>,
as well as <s>Mattaskhalitaka</s> and <s>Madādvilasita</s>,
<s>Gatimaṇḍalaka</s> is to be known, and likewise <s>Paricchinna</s>,
then there is <s>Parivṛttacita</s>, and also <s>Vaiśākharecita</s>,
then <s>Parāvṛtta</s> is to be known, and likewise <s>Alātaka</s>,
then <s>Pārśvaccheda</s> is taught, and likewise <s>Vidyudbhrānta</s>,
and <s>Ūrūdvṛtta</s>, and there is also <s>Ālīḍha</s>,
and <s>Recita</s> is to be known, and likewise <s>Acchurita</s> is remembered,
and <s>Ākṣiptarecita</s>, and another is <s>Saṃbhrānta</s>,
while <s>Apasarpa</s> is to be known, and also <s>Ardhanikuṭṭaka</s>.
These thirty-two <s>aṅgahāras</s> have been stated by name.
Now I shall explain their use as based on <s>karaṇas</s>,
and how the movement of hands and feet is to be arranged by performers.

children.text: aṅgahāreṣu vakṣyāmi karaṇeṣu ca vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: I shall speak about the <s>aṅgahāras</s> and the <s>karaṇas</s>, O twice-borns,
because the accomplishment of all <s>aṅgahāras</s> comes from <s>karaṇas</s>.
Therefore I shall explain them by name and also by action.
The combination of hands and feet is a <s>karaṇa</s> of dance.
Two <s>nṛttakaraṇas</s> (pure-dance units) become a <s>nṛttamātṛkā</s>.
And an <s>aṅgahāra</s> is formed with two, three, or four such <s>mātṛkās</s>.

children.text: tribhiḥ kalāpakaṃ caiva caturbhiḥ ṣaṇḍakaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: With three there is a <s>kalāpaka</s>, and with four there is a <s>ṣaṇḍaka</s>.

children.text: pañcaiva karaṇāni syuḥ saṅghātaka iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Five <s>karaṇas</s> are remembered as a <s>saṅghātaka</s>.
Or with six, or with seven, and likewise with eight or nine.
The <s>aṅgahāras</s> (limb-sequences) are taught here as joined with <s>karaṇas</s> (dance units).
I shall describe the arrangement of hands and feet for these very ones.
First come <s>talapuṣpapuṭa</s>, <s>vartita</s>, and <s>valitoru</s>.
<s>apaviddha</s>, <s>samanakha</s>, <s>līna</s>, and <s>svastikarecita</s>;
and <s>maṇḍalasvastika</s>, then also <s>nikuṭṭaka</s>;
likewise <s>ardhanikuṭṭa</s> and also <s>kaṭicchinna</s>;
and <s>ardharecitaka</s>, and also <s>vakṣaḥsvastika</s>;
<s>unmatta</s>, <s>svastika</s>, and likewise <s>pṛṣṭhasvastika</s>;
<s>diksvastika</s>, <s>alāta</s>, and likewise <s>kaṭīsama</s>;
<s>ākṣiptarecita</s>, and likewise <s>vikṣiptākṣiptaka</s>;
<s>ardhasvastika</s> is specified, and next <s>añcita</s>;
<s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s> is taught, and likewise <s>ūrdhvajānu</s>;

children.text: nikuñcitaṃ ca mattalli tvardhamattalli caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: and <s>nikuñcita</s>, <s>mattalli</s>, and indeed <s>ardhamattalli</s>;
there is <s>recakanikkuṭṭa</s>, and likewise <s>pādāpaviddhaka</s>;

children.text: valitaṃ ghūrṇitaṃ caiva lalitaṃ ca tathāparam ||
children.translated_text: <s>valita</s>, <s>ghūrṇita</s>, and then also <s>lalita</s>;
and likewise <s>daṇḍapakṣa</s> and <s>bhujaṅgatrastarecita</s>;
<s>nūpura</s> is also declared, and likewise <s>vaiśākharecita</s>;
<s>bhramara</s>, <s>catura</s>, and also <s>bhujaṅgāñcita</s>;
and <s>daṇḍarecitaka</s>, and likewise <s>vṛścikakuṭṭita</s>;
and also <s>kaṭibhrānta</s> and <s>latāvṛścika</s>;

children.text: chinnaṃ ca karaṇaṃ proktaṃ tathā vṛścikarecitam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>chinna</s> karaṇa is taught, and likewise <s>vṛścikarecita</s>;
<s>vṛścika</s>, <s>vyaṃsita</s>, and likewise <s>pārśvanikuṭṭaka</s>;
<s>lalāṭatilaka</s>, <s>krānta</s>, <s>kuñcita</s>, and <s>cakramaṇḍala</s>;
<s>uromaṇḍala</s>, <s>ākṣipta</s>, and likewise <s>talavilāsita</s>;
<s>argala</s>, then <s>vikṣipta</s>, <s>āvṛtta</s>, and <s>dolapādaka</s>;
<s>vivṛtta</s>, <s>vinivṛtta</s>, <s>pārśvakrānta</s>, and <s>niśumbhita</s>;
<s>vidyutbhrānta</s>, <s>atikrānta</s>, and also <s>vivartitaka</s>;
and <s>gajakrīḍitaka</s>, and likewise <s>talasaṃsphoṭita</s>;
and <s>garuḍaplutaka</s>, and then <s>gaṇḍasūci</s>;
<s>parivṛtta</s> is specified, and likewise <s>pārśvajānu</s>;
and <s>gṛdhrāvalīnaka</s>, <s>sannata</s>, and also <s>sūcī</s>;
the karaṇa called <s>ardhasūci</s>, and likewise <s>sūcividdha</s>;
<s>apakrānta</s> is declared, and likewise <s>mayūralalita</s>;
<s>sarpita</s>, <s>daṇḍapāda</s>, and also <s>hariṇapluta</s>;
<s>preṅkholita</s>, <s>nitamba</s>, <s>skhalita</s>, and <s>karihastaka</s>;
<s>prasarpitaka</s> is specified, and likewise <s>siṃhavikrīḍita</s>;
<s>siṃhākarṣita</s>, <s>udvṛtta</s>, and likewise <s>upasṛta</s>;
and <s>talasaṃghaṭṭita</s>, <s>janita</s>, and <s>āvahitthaka</s>;
<s>niveśa</s>, <s>elakākrīḍa</s>, and likewise <s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>;
and <s>madaskhalitaka</s>, and also <s>viṣṇukrānta</s>;
then <s>sambhrānta</s>, <s>viṣkambha</s>, and also <s>udghaṭṭita</s>;
and <s>vṛṣabhakrīḍita</s>, and then also <s>lolita</s>;
and <s>nāgāpasarpita</s>, and likewise <s>śakaṭāsya</s>;
and <s>gaṅgāvataraṇa</s>; thus one hundred and eight have been stated.
This set of one hundred and eight <s>karaṇas</s> has indeed been taught by me.

children.text: nṛtye yuddhe niyuddhe ca tathā gatiparikrame
children.translated_text: In dance, in battle, in hand-to-hand combat, and in the circuits of gait,
I shall describe the arrangement of battle <s>cārīs</s> in the exposition of movement.
Wherever appropriate, they should be combined by teachers according to the capability of <s>nāṭya</s> (dramatic performance).

children.text: prāyeṇa karaṇe kāryo vāmo vakṣaḥsthitaḥ karaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the most part, in a <s>karaṇa</s> the left hand should be placed at the chest,
and the right hand should follow the foot.
Now listen to the movement of hands and feet, joined with waist, side, and thigh,
and furnished with chest, back, and belly, as it is about to be described.
The stances, the <s>cārīs</s>, and likewise the dance-hands,
are to be known as the matrix; through their combination a <s>karaṇa</s> comes into being.
Where the waist is aligned with the ears, and the elbows, shoulders, and head likewise,
and the chest is raised, that is called <s>sauṣṭhava</s> (proper carriage).
With a <s>puṣpapuṭa</s> hand on the left side, the foot moving on the front of the sole,

children.text: tathā ca saṃnataṃ pārśvaṃ talapuṣpapuṭaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: and the side similarly bent down, it becomes <s>talapuṣpapuṭa</s>.
When the wrists are bent and the two hands are turned outward and around,

children.text: hastau nipatitau corvorvartitaṃ karaṇaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and fall upon the thighs, that <s>karaṇa</s> is <s>vartita</s>.
When the two hands in <s>śukatuṇḍa</s> are turned outward and around,
and the thighs are turned in it, it is called <s>valitoruka</s>.
Having turned the hand called <s>śukatuṇḍa</s>, one should drop it on the back of the thigh,
while the left hand is placed at the chest; that becomes <s>apaviddha</s>.

children.text: śliṣṭau samanakhau padau karau cāpi pralambitau ||
children.translated_text: Where the feet are joined, the toenails level, and the hands are hanging down,

children.text: dehaḥ svābhāviko yatra bhavetsamanakhaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and the body is in its natural state, that is <s>samanakha</s>.
With <s>patāka</s> and <s>añjali</s> at the chest, and the neck extended,
and with the shoulder-joints lowered, that <s>karaṇa</s> is remembered as <s>līna</s>.
Where the crossed hands, in <s>recita</s> and <s>āviddha</s>, are separated and placed at the waist,
that <s>karaṇa</s> is to be known by the learned as <s>svastikarecita</s>.

children.text: svastikau tu karau kṛtvā prāṅmukhordhvatalau samau ||
children.translated_text: Having made the two hands crossed, equal, facing forward with upward palms,

children.text: tathā ca maṇḍalaṃ sthānaṃ maṇḍalasvastikaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and likewise assuming the <s>maṇḍala</s> stance, that is <s>maṇḍalasvastika</s>.
When the hands are <s>nikuṭṭita</s> between their own arms and head,

children.text: pādau nikuṭṭitau caiva jñeyaṃ tattu nikuṭṭakam
children.translated_text: and the feet are likewise <s>nikuṭṭita</s>, that should be known as <s>nikuṭṭaka</s>.
When the hands are <s>añcita</s> at the shoulders, with fingers facing inward,
with a half-combination of <s>nikuñcita</s>, it becomes <s>ardhanikuṭṭaka</s>.
The waist is cut alternately, with the two <s>pallava</s> hands at the shoulder-tops ...
And when the <s>karaṇa</s> is done again and again, that becomes <s>Kaṭicchinna</s>;
the hand is thrown aside in the <s>sūcī</s> form, and the foot is likewise stamped.

children.text: saṃnataṃ yatra pārśvaṃ ca tadbhaved ardharecitam
children.translated_text: Where the side is bent down, that becomes <s>Ardharecita</s>.

children.text: svastikau caraṇau yatra karau vakṣasi recitau ||
children.translated_text: Where the feet are in <s>svastika</s> and the hands are waved at the chest,
and the chest is contracted, that indeed is <s>Vakṣaḥsvastika</s>.

children.text: añcitena tu pādena recitau tu karau yadā ||
children.translated_text: But when, with an <s>añcita</s> foot, the two hands are waved,
that <s>karaṇa</s> should be known by experts in dance as <s>Unmatta</s>.
When there are <s>svastika</s> formations with both hands and feet,
that <s>karaṇa</s> is called <s>Svastika</s> by those who seek the <s>karaṇa</s>s.
When the feet are crossed while the arms are stretched out and drawn back,
with <s>Apakrānta</s> and <s>Ardhasūcī</s>, that becomes <s>Pṛṣṭhasvastika</s>.
Where the hand is joined closely at the two sides and also in front,
with hands and feet in <s>svastika</s>, that is called <s>Diksvastika</s>.
Having made the foot <s>alāta</s>, one should throw the right hand aside;
one should perform the sequence of the raised knee: it is remembered as <s>Alātaka</s>.
The foot has moved away from <s>svastika</s>, and the hands are placed at the navel and hip;
the side too is raised: that <s>karaṇa</s> is <s>Kaṭīsama</s>.
The left hand should be at the heart, while the other is drawn back and waved;
waved and thrown aside, that is <s>Ākṣiptarecita</s>.
Where the hand and foot are thrown outward, and then that same motion is drawn back again,
that <s>karaṇa</s> should be known as <s>Vikṣiptākṣiptaka</s>, O twice-born ones.

children.text: svastikau caraṇau kṛtvā karihastaṃ ca dakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the feet in <s>svastika</s> and made the right hand a <s>karihasta</s>,
with the left likewise at the chest, one should designate it <s>Ardhasvastika</s>.

children.text: vyāvṛttaparivṛttastu sa eva tu karo yadā ||
children.translated_text: When that same hand is turned outward and turned around,
and is <s>añcita</s> at the tip of the nose, that is called <s>Añcita</s>.
Having raised a bent foot, one should turn the thigh into a triangular shape;
from the turning of hip and knee arises <s>Bhujaṅgatrāsita</s>.
Having raised a bent foot, one should place the knee level with the breast;
the two hands follow the requirements of performance: this is proclaimed as <s>Ūrdhvajānu</s>.

children.text: vṛścikaṃ caraṇaṃ kṛtvā karaṃ pārśve nikuñcayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the foot <s>vṛścika</s>, one should bend the hand at the side,

children.text: nāsāgre dakṣiṇaṃ caiva jñeyaṃ tattu nikuñcitam
children.translated_text: and the right hand at the tip of the nose; that should be known as <s>Nikuñcita</s>.
With circling approaches by the left and right feet,
and with hands twisted upward and thrown aside, it is called <s>Mattallī</s>.
The feet are slipped and moved aside, and the left hand is waved;
the other hand should be at the hip: that is remembered as <s>Ardhamattallī</s>.

children.text: recito dakṣiṇo hastaḥ pādaḥ savyo nikuṭṭitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The right hand is waved, and the left foot is stamped;
