the left hand is in <s>dolā</s>: that is <s>Recitanikuṭṭita</s>.
The hands should be at the navel region, facing forward, in <s>khaṭakāmukha</s>;
the feet are pierced in <s>sūcī</s> and moved in <s>apakrānta</s> in <s>Pādāpaviddhaka</s>.
The hand should be thrown aside, and the foot likewise in <s>sūcī</s>;

children.text: tathā trikaṃ vivṛttaṃ ca valitaṃ nāma tadbhavet
children.translated_text: and when the hips are turned and curved, that is named <s>Valita</s>.
One hand is rotated and whirled, and the left hand is swung;

children.text: svastikāpasṛtaḥ pādaḥ karaṇaṃ ghūrṇitaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: the foot has moved away from <s>svastika</s>: that <s>karaṇa</s> is <s>Ghūrṇita</s>.
The left hand should be a <s>karihasta</s>, and the right hand turned around;

children.text: bahuśaḥ kuṭṭitaḥ pādo jñeyaṃ tallalitaṃ budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: the foot is stamped many times: that is known by the wise as <s>Lalita</s>.
Having formed <s>Ūrdhvajānu</s>, one should place the <s>latā</s> above it;
that <s>karaṇa</s> is called <s>Daṇḍapakṣa</s> by those who know dance.
Where, after making <s>Bhujaṅgatrāsita</s>, both hands are also waved,
with the hands positioned on the left side, it is <s>Bhujaṅgatrastarecita</s>.
Having made the hips well curved, with the hands in <s>Latārecitaka</s>,

children.text: nūpuraśca tathā pādaḥ karaṇe nūpure nyaset
children.translated_text: and likewise with the foot as <s>Nūpura</s>, one should set it in the <s>Nūpura</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: recitau hastapādau ca kaṭī grīvā ca recitā ||
children.translated_text: The hands and feet are waved, and the hip and neck are also waved;
with the <s>Vaiśākha</s> stance, this becomes <s>Vaiśākharecita</s>.

children.text: ākṣiptaḥ svastikaḥ pādaḥ karau codveṣṭitau tathā ||
children.translated_text: The foot is drawn back in <s>svastika</s>, and the hands are likewise twisted upward;

children.text: trikasya valanāccaiva jñeyaṃ bhramarakaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and from the turning of the hips, that should be known as <s>Bhramaraka</s>.

children.text: añcitaḥ syātkaro vāmaḥ savyaścatura eva tu ||
children.translated_text: The left hand should be <s>añcita</s>, and the other hand exactly <s>catura</s>;
the right foot is stamped: that is proclaimed as <s>Catura</s>.
The right foot is <s>Bhujaṅgatrāsita</s>, and the right hand is waved;
the left hand is called <s>Latā</s>: this becomes <s>Bhujaṅgāñcitaka</s>.
Where the hand and foot are stretched out on every side like a staff,
and are waved, that indeed should be known as the <s>Daṇḍakarecita</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.
Having made the foot <s>vṛścika</s>, both hands should then be stamped or struck down;
that should be known as <s>Vṛścikakuṭṭita</s>.

children.text: sūciṃ kṛtvāpaviddhaṃ ca dakṣiṇaṃ caraṇaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having made <s>sūcī</s> and thrown it aside, one should place the right foot;
where the hip is waved, that is called <s>Kaṭibhrānta</s>.
The foot is bent backward, with the sole and toes curved upward;

children.text: latākhyaśca karo vāmas tal latāvṛścikaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: the left hand is called <s>Latā</s>: that becomes <s>Latāvṛścika</s>.
An <s>Alapadma</s> is at the region of the hip, and the hip is cut alternately;
with the <s>Vaiśākha</s> stance here, that becomes the <s>Chinna</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.

children.text: vṛścikaṃ caraṇaṃ kṛtvā svastikau ca karāvubhau ||
children.translated_text: Having made the foot <s>vṛścika</s>, with both hands in <s>svastika</s>,
the hands are waved and spread apart: this is <s>Vṛścikarecita</s>.
The hands are bent toward the shoulders and head, and the foot is likewise bent backward;
with the back deeply bowed, that is proclaimed as <s>Vṛścika</s>.

children.text: ālīḍhaṃ sthānakaṃ yatra karau vakṣasi recitau ||
children.translated_text: Where there is the <s>Ālīḍha</s> stance and the hands are waved at the chest,

children.text: ūrdhvādho viprakīrṇau ca vyaṃsitaṃ karaṇaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and spread upward and downward, that <s>karaṇa</s> is <s>Vyaṃsita</s>.

children.text: hastau tu svastikau pārśve tathā pādo nikuṭṭitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The two hands are in the <s>svastika</s> position at the side, and the foot is likewise in <s>nikuṭṭita</s>.
Where this occurs, that <s>karaṇa</s> is to be known by the wise as <s>pārśvanikuṭṭita</s>.
Having made the foot into the <s>vṛścika</s> (scorpion) position, then with the big toe of the foot
one should make a mark on the forehead; that is <s>lalāṭatilaka</s>.
Having made it bent behind, and then the crossing step,

children.text: ākṣiptau ca karau kāryau krāntake karaṇe dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: the two hands should be thrown out in the <s>krāntaka</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, O twice-born ones.

children.text: ādyaḥ pādo nataḥ kāryaḥ savyahastaśca kuñcitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first foot should be made bent, and the left hand should be curved;
when it is open and placed on the left side, that is called <s>kuñcita</s>.
With both arms hanging down and with the body bent forward,
when there is an inward-thrown movement, that is to be known as <s>cakramaṇḍala</s>.
When the feet move apart from <s>svastika</s> and follow the <s>apaviddha</s> step,
and the hands make circles at the chest, that is <s>uromaṇḍalika</s>.

children.text: ākṣiptaṃ hastapādaṃ ca kriyate yatra vegataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where the hand and foot are thrown out swiftly,
that <s>karaṇa</s> is to be understood as called <s>ākṣipta</s>, O best of twice-born ones.
The foot, with toes and sole turned upward, is stretched upward to the side;
one should make the hands with curved palms in <s>talavilāsita</s>.

children.text: pṛṣṭhataḥ prasṛtaḥ pādo dvau tālāvardhameva ca ||
children.translated_text: The foot is stretched out behind, by two and a half <s>tālas</s>,

children.text: tasyaiva cānugo hastaḥ puratastvargalaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and the hand follows that very foot, while the other is in front; that is <s>argala</s>.

children.text: vikṣiptaṃ hastapādaṃ ca pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvato 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: Where the hand and foot are cast out behind or to the side,
moving along a single path, that is called <s>vikṣipta</s>.
Having stretched out the bent foot, one should quickly turn it back again;
the hands follow the requirements of the performance; that is called <s>āvarta</s>.
Having raised the bent foot, one should swing it from side to side;
the hands follow the requirements of the performance; that is called <s>ḍolāpāda</s>.

children.text: ākṣiptaṃ hastapādaṃ ca trikaṃ caiva vivartayet ||
children.translated_text: The hand and foot are thrown out, and the <s>trika</s> (hip-joint region) should be turned about;

children.text: recitau ca tathā hastau vivṛtte karaṇe dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: the hands are likewise <s>recita</s> in the <s>vivṛtta</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, O twice-born ones.
Having performed <s>sūcīviddha</s>, one should then turn the <s>trika</s> back;

children.text: karau ca recitau kāryau vinivṛtte dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: the hands should be made <s>recita</s> in <s>vinivṛtta</s>, O best of twice-born ones.
Having made the <s>pārśvakrānta</s> step, one should then let the foot fall in front;
the hands follow the requirements of the performance; that is called <s>pārśvakrānta</s>.
The foot is bent behind, and the chest is raised;
the hand should be placed in <s>tilaka</s>; that is called <s>nistambhita</s>.
One should stretch out the foot, bent from behind, so that it brushes the head;
with a circular sweep on all sides, that is called <s>vidyudbhrānta</s>.
Having made the <s>atikrānta</s> step, one should stretch the foot out in front;
the hands follow the requirements of the performance; it is proclaimed as <s>atikrānta</s>.

children.text: ākṣiptaṃ hastapādaṃ ca trikaṃ caiva vivartitam ||
children.translated_text: The hand and foot are thrown out, and the <s>trika</s> is turned about;
the second hand is <s>recita</s>; that indeed is <s>vivartitaka</s>.
The left hand is curved at the ear, and the right is a <s>latāhasta</s> (creeper-hand);
with the <s>ḍolāpāda</s> as well, it becomes <s>gajakrīḍitaka</s>.
Having quickly lifted the foot, one should then let it fall in front;
the hands are made to clap palm against palm; this is regarded as <s>talasaṃsphoṭita</s>.
The foot is stretched backward, and the hands are in <s>latā</s> and <s>recita</s>;
the head is also raised; it becomes <s>garuḍaplutaka</s>.
There is a <s>sūcīpāda</s> (needle-foot), the side is bent, and one hand is placed at the chest;
the second is curved at the cheek; that is called <s>gaṇḍasūcī</s>.
The hands are wound upward, and the <s>sūcīpāda</s> is turned about;
the <s>trika</s> is also turned around; that is called <s>parivṛtta</s>.
One foot stands evenly, while the other is placed on the back of the thigh;
and a fist-hand is placed at the chest; that is called <s>pārśvajānu</s>.
The foot is stretched backward, and the knee is slightly curved;
where the two arms are extended, that becomes <s>gṛdhrāvalīnaka</s>.
Having leapt up, the two feet should be made to stand in <s>svastika</s> in front;

children.text: saṃnatau ca tathā hastau saṃnataṃ tadudāhṛtam
children.translated_text: the hands are likewise bent down; that is called <s>saṃnata</s>.
Having raised the bent foot, one should set it on the ground in front;
the hands follow the requirements of the performance; that is termed <s>sūcī</s>.
The hand at the head is <s>alapadma</s>, and the right foot is <s>sūcīpāda</s>;
where this occurs, that <s>karaṇa</s> is to be known by the name <s>ardhasūcī</s>.
When the second foot is pierced by the needle-like foot,
with the hands placed at the waist and chest, that is called <s>sūcīviddha</s>.
Having made the foot turned around the thigh, one should place it down with the <s>apakrānta</s> step;
the hands follow the requirements of the performance; that is called <s>apakrānta</s>.

children.text: vṛścikaṃ caraṇaṃ kṛtvā recitau ca tathā karau ||
children.translated_text: Having made the foot into the <s>vṛścika</s> position, and likewise the hands <s>recita</s>,

children.text: tathā trikaṃ vivṛttaṃ ca mayūralalitaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: and with the <s>trika</s> also turned, it becomes <s>mayūralalita</s>.
The feet are curved and drawn apart, and the head is moved around;
the hands are likewise <s>recita</s>; that is called <s>sarpita</s>.
Having made the foot into <s>nūpura</s>, one should stretch out the staff-like foot;
and the hand is swiftly thrown; that is called <s>daṇḍapāda</s>.
Having made the <s>atikrānta</s> step, one should leap up and come down;
with the bent lower leg thrown upward, one should know that as <s>hariṇapluta</s>.
Having made the <s>ḍolāpāda</s> step, one should leap up and come down;
the <s>trika</s> is also turned around; that is called <s>preṅkholita</s>.
The arms are extended upward, and the hands have their fingers facing one another;

children.text: baddhā cārī tathā caiva nitambe karaṇe bhavet
children.translated_text: the <s>cārī</s> is likewise <s>baddhā</s>; this is the <s>nitamba</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.
Having made the <s>dolāpāda</s> step, both hands follow it;

children.text: recitau ghūrṇitau vāpi skhalitaṃ karaṇaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: whether <s>recita</s> or whirling, the <s>karaṇa</s> becomes <s>skhalita</s>.
One hand is placed at the chest, and the other has its palm twisted around;
and a bent foot is to be employed in <s>karihastaka</s>.

children.text: ekastu recito hasto latākhyastu tathā paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: One hand is in <s>recita</s>, and the other is likewise called <s>latā</s>;
with the feet extended with their soles spreading, that is precisely <s>prasarpitaka</s>.

children.text: alātaṃ ca puraḥkṛtvā dvitīyaṃ ca drutakramam ||
children.translated_text: Having first made <s>alāta</s>, and then a second quick step,
with the hands also following the feet, these are remembered in <s>siṃhavikrīḍita</s>.
The foot is extended behind, and likewise the two hands are contracted;
then they should again be made in just that way in <s>siṃhākarṣitaka</s>, O twice-born ones.
With the hand thrown out, the body thrown out, and the foot thrown out,
and with the limbs turned upward, this <s>karaṇa</s> is remembered as <s>udvṛtta</s>.
One foot is thrown out, and the hands follow that very foot;

children.text: ānataṃ ca tathā gātraṃ tathopasṛtakaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: the body is also bent down, and thus it becomes <s>upasṛtaka</s>.
Having made the swinging-foot step, with the two hands struck palm to palm,
one should always make the left hand <s>recita</s> in <s>talasaṃghaṭṭita</s>.
One hand is placed at the chest, and the second hangs down;
the foot is set on the tip of the sole in the <s>janita</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.
Having made the <s>janita</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, with the hands whose fingers face one another,
and with them slowly lowered, that should be known as <s>avahitthaka</s>.
The hands should be placed at the chest, and the breast should be drawn in;

children.text: maṇḍalasthānakaṃ caiva niveśaṃ karaṇaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: with a <s>maṇḍala</s> stance, that <s>karaṇa</s> is <s>niveśa</s>.
With the feet in <s>talasañcāra</s>, there is a leap and a fall;

children.text: saṃnataṃ valitaṃ gātram elakākrīḍitaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: the body is bent and turned, and that is <s>elakākrīḍita</s>.
Having made the hand perform <s>āvṛtta</s>, one should set it bent on the back of the thigh;
the shank is bent and likewise turned upward; that is <s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>.
The two hands should hang down, and the head should be swung around;
the feet are turned and flung out in <s>madaskhalitaka</s>, O twice-born ones.
The foot is stretched forward, bent, and facing upward toward the sky;

children.text: karau ca recitau yatra viṣṇukrāntaṃ taducyate
children.translated_text: where the two hands are in <s>recita</s>, that is called <s>Viṣṇukrānta</s>.
Having made the hand turn around, one should bend it on the back of the thigh;

children.text: ūruścaiva tathāviddhaḥ saṃbhrāntaṃ karaṇaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: and the thigh is likewise flung out; that <s>karaṇa</s> is <s>saṃbhrānta</s>.
The hand is cast away with the <s>sūcī</s> gesture, and the foot is stamped;

children.text: vakṣaḥsthaśca karo vāmo viṣkambhe karaṇe bhavet
children.translated_text: and the left hand is at the chest in the <s>viṣkambha</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.
The feet should be made <s>udghaṭṭita</s>, and the hands should be struck palm to palm;

children.text: nataṃ ca pārśvaṃ kartavyaṃ budhairudghaṭṭite sadā
children.translated_text: the side should always be bent by the wise in <s>udghaṭṭita</s>.

children.text: prayujyālātakaṃ pūrvaṃ hastau cāpi hi recayet ||
children.translated_text: Having first employed <s>alātaka</s>, one should also make the hands <s>recita</s>;
they are bent and curved in <s>vṛṣabhakrīḍita</s> each time.
The hands are <s>recita</s> and curved, and the head is swaying and turned;
where this is done on both sides, that is declared to be <s>lolita</s>.
The feet are crossed and drawn apart, and the head is swung around;

children.text: recitau ca tathā hastau syātāṃ nāgāpasarpite
children.translated_text: and likewise the hands should be <s>recita</s> in <s>nāgāpasarpita</s>.
With the body lowered, extending the foot in <s>talasañcāra</s>,
and making the chest raised up, one should employ <s>śakaṭāsya</s>.
The feet have their toes and soles turned upward, and the hands are downward-facing <s>tripatākā</s>;

children.text: hastau śiraḥ saṃnataṃ ca gaṅgāvataraṇaṃ tviti
children.translated_text: with the head bent down, this is called <s>Gaṅgāvataraṇa</s>.

children.text: yāni sthānāni yāścāryo vyāyāme kathitāni tu ||
children.translated_text: The stances and the <s>cārīs</s> that have been taught in exercise,
these are to be the foot movements of these <s>karaṇas</s>.
And the dance-hands that were stated in the practice of <s>nṛtta</s>,
their combination is to be understood, in brief, within the <s>karaṇas</s>.

children.text: prāyeṇa karaṇe kāryo vāmo vakṣaḥsthitaḥ karaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the most part, in a <s>karaṇa</s>, the left hand should be placed at the chest;
and the right hand should also follow the foot.

children.text: cāryaścaiva tu yāḥ proktā nṛttahastāstathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>cārīs</s> that have been described, and likewise the dance-hands,
are to be understood as the <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrix); through their variations there are the <s>karaṇas</s>.
This set of one hundred and eight <s>karaṇas</s> has now been stated by me;
after this I shall explain the arrangement of the <s>aṅgahāras</s>.
Having stretched out and raised the two hands, one should employ <s>samapāda</s>;
one should extend the left hand upward in <s>vyaṃsita-apasṛta</s>.

children.text: pratyālīḍhaṃ tataḥ kuryāt tathaiva ca nikuṭṭakam ||
children.translated_text: Then one should perform <s>pratyālīḍha</s>, and likewise <s>nikuṭṭaka</s>;
then one should perform <s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>, then <s>ākṣipta</s> and <s>svastika</s>.

children.text: nitambaṃ kari hastaṃ ca kaṭicchinnaṃ ca yogataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and <s>kaṭicchinna</s>, in proper combination;
this <s>aṅgahāra</s>, with a steady hand, is <s>Harapriya</s>.
The two, <s>talapuṣpa</s> and <s>apaviddha</s>, then <s>vartita</s> together with <s>nikuṭṭika</s>;
<s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>, likewise <s>ākṣipta</s>, and also <s>uromaṇḍala</s>;

children.text: nitambaṃ karihastaṃ ca kaṭicchinnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>kaṭicchinna</s>;
this is the <s>aṅgahāra</s> named <s>Paryastaka</s>, born from <s>Hara</s>.
Having performed <s>alapallava</s> and <s>sūcī</s>, and then <s>vikṣipta</s>,
one should next perform <s>āvartita</s>, and likewise <s>nikuṭṭaka</s>.
<s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>, likewise <s>ākṣipta</s>, and also <s>uromaṇḍala</s>;
<s>karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s>: this becomes <s>Sūcīviddha</s>.

children.text: apaviddhaṃ tu karaṇaṃ sūcīviddhaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>apaviddha</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, and likewise <s>sūcīviddha</s>;
with a hand in <s>udveṣṭita</s>, one should turn the <s>trika</s> (lower torso).
The two hands are in <s>uromaṇḍala</s>, and likewise there is <s>kaṭicchinna</s>;
this <s>aṅgahāra</s> should be known by performers as <s>Apaviddha</s>.
Having performed the <s>nūpura</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, then <s>vikṣipta</s> and <s>alātaka</s>,
one should again perform <s>ākṣiptaka</s>, and likewise <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>.

children.text: nitambaṃ karihastaṃ ca kaṭicchinnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>kaṭicchinna</s>;
that <s>aṅgahāra</s> should be known by performers as <s>Ākṣiptaka</s>.
The hand is <s>udveṣṭita</s> and <s>apaviddha</s>, and the foot is <s>nikuṭṭita</s>;
Then again, by that same combination, it should be done on the left side.
The two hands are <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>; <s>nitamba</s> and <s>karihastaka</s> are also used.
Together with <s>kaṭicchinna</s>, it should always be performed in the dance called <s>Uddhaṭṭita</s>.
The two hands are alternately <s>udveṣṭita</s>, and the two feet are <s>nikuṭṭita</s>.
They are bent and curved, and likewise there is <s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>.

children.text: caturaśraṃ karaṃ kṛtvā pādena ca nikuṭṭakam ||
children.translated_text: Having made the hand <s>caturaśra</s>, one should make <s>nikuṭṭaka</s> with the foot.
Also <s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s>, and again the hand in <s>udviṣṭita</s>, are used.

children.text: paricchinnaṃ ca kartavyaṃ trikaṃ bhramarakeṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paricchinna</s> should be performed, while the <s>trika</s> (lower torso) is moved with <s>bhramaraka</s>.
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> are declared in <s>Viṣkambha</s>.

children.text: daṇḍapādaṃ karaṃ caiva vikṣipyākṣipya caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: One should make <s>daṇḍapāda</s>, and also cast out and draw in the hand.

children.text: vyaṃsitaṃ vāmahastaṃ ca saha pādena sarpayet
children.translated_text: One should make the left hand <s>vyaṃsita</s> and glide it together with the foot.
A pair of <s>nikuṭṭaka</s>s should be made, and <s>ākṣipta</s> with the chest in <s>maṇḍala</s>.
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> should be performed in <s>Aparājita</s>.
Having performed the <s>kuṭṭita</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, and likewise <s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s>,
with a <s>recita</s> hand one should indicate the <s>patāka</s> hand.
one should employ <s>ākṣiptaka</s> and likewise <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>.
The hand called <s>latā</s>, together with <s>kaṭicchinna</s>, occurs in <s>Viṣkambhāpasṛta</s>.

children.text: trikaṃ suvalitaṃ kṛtvā nūpuraṃ karaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>trika</s> well turned, and also the <s>nūpura</s> <s>karaṇa</s>,
one should perform <s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s> on the left, and likewise <s>vaiśākharecita</s>.

children.text: ākṣiptakaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā paricchinnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, having performed <s>ākṣiptaka</s>, and likewise <s>paricchinna</s>,
one should make <s>bāhyabhramaraka</s> and <s>uromaṇḍala</s>.

children.text: nitambaṃ karihastaṃ ca kaṭicchinnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>kaṭicchinna</s> are used.
This is the <s>aṅgahāra</s> <s>Mattākrīḍa</s>, dear to <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: recitaṃ hastapādaṃ ca kṛtvā vṛścikameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Having made the hand and foot <s>recita</s>, and also <s>vṛścika</s>,
one should again apply <s>vṛścika</s> by that same combination.
And <s>nikuṭṭaka</s> is made to the left and to the right in sequence.
The movement called <s>latā</s>, with <s>kaṭiccheda</s>, occurs in <s>Svastikarecita</s>.

children.text: pārśve tu svastikaṃ baddhvā kāryaṃ tvatha nikuṭṭakam ||
children.translated_text: Having formed <s>svastika</s> at the side, <s>nikuṭṭaka</s> should then be performed.

children.text: dvitīyasya ca pārśvasya vidhiḥ syādyameva hi
children.translated_text: The rule for the second side should be exactly the same.
Then, turning the hand around, one should bring it down on the back of the thigh.
After that one should make <s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>, and again <s>ākṣipta</s>.

children.text: nitambaṃ karihastaṃ ca kaṭicchinnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>kaṭicchinna</s> are used.
This is proclaimed as the <s>aṅgahāra</s> <s>Pārśvasvastika</s>.

children.text: vṛścikaṃ karaṇaṃ kṛtvā latākhyaṃ hastameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the <s>vṛścika</s> <s>karaṇa</s> and the hand called <s>latā</s>,

children.text: tameva ca karaṃ bhūyo nāsāgre sannikuñcayet
children.translated_text: one should again bend that very hand at the tip of the nose.
Making that same hand <s>udveṣṭita</s>, one should turn the <s>nitamba</s> (hip).
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> occur in <s>Vṛścikāpasṛta</s>.
Having made <s>nūpurapāda</s>, and likewise <s>ākṣiptaka</s>,

children.text: paricchinnaṃ ca kartavyaṃ sūcīpādaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>paricchinna</s> should be performed, and likewise <s>sūcīpāda</s>.
<s>Nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and also <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s> are likewise used.

children.text: kaṭīcchinnaṃ tataścaiva bhramaraḥ sa tu saṃjñitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>kaṭicchinna</s> also; this is named <s>Bhramara</s>.
Having performed the <s>matalli</s> <s>karaṇa</s> and turned the right hand,
it should be properly bent in the region of the cheek.
<s>Apaviddha</s> and <s>druta</s> are joined with <s>talasaṃsphoṭa</s> (palm-striking).
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> occur in <s>Mattaskhalitaka</s>.
With swinging, moving hands, and with feet moving apart from <s>svastika</s>,
and likewise with hands bent, turned, and struck palm to palm,
<s>nikuṭṭita</s> should be performed, and likewise <s>ūrūdvṛtta</s>.
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> occur in <s>Madādvilasita</s>.

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ sthānakaṃ kṛtvā tathā hastau ca recitau ||
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> stance and the two hands <s>recita</s>,
with a foot in <s>udghaṭṭita</s>, there is the <s>mattalli</s> <s>karaṇa</s>.
The <s>ākṣipta</s> <s>karaṇa</s> and also <s>uromaṇḍala</s>
and likewise <s>kaṭicchinna</s> occur in <s>Gatimaṇḍala</s>.
One should employ <s>samapāda</s>, and immediately afterward <s>paricchinna</s>.
With the foot in <s>āviddha</s>, one should also perform <s>bāhyabhramaraka</s>.
With the left <s>sūcī</s>, <s>atikrānta</s>, and likewise <s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s> are used.
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> are prescribed in <s>Paricchinna</s>.
The two hands, crossed as <s>svastika</s> and then released, should be placed above the head.

children.text: tataḥ savyaṃ karaṃ cāpi gātramānamya recayet
children.translated_text: Then, bending the body, one should make the left hand <s>recita</s>.
Again there, raising the body, one should lift it in <s>recita</s>.

children.text: latākhyau ca karau kṛtvā vṛścikaṃ samprayojayet
children.translated_text: Having made the two hands called <s>latā</s>, one should apply <s>vṛścika</s>.
<s>Recita</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s> are used.
One should employ <s>ākṣiptaka</s> and also a <s>svastika</s> of the feet.
Here again the procedure when facing backward should be exactly the same.
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> occur in <s>Parivṛttakarecita</s>.

children.text: recitau saha gātreṇa hyapaviddhau karau yadā ||
children.translated_text: When the two hands are <s>recita</s> and <s>apaviddha</s> together with the body,
again in that same place, raising the body, one should make <s>recita</s>.
One should make <s>nūpurapāda</s> and likewise <s>bhujaṅgatrāsita</s>.
One should bend <s>recita</s> and <s>maṇḍala</s> at the shoulder.
<s>Ūrūdvṛtta</s>, likewise <s>ākṣipta</s>, and also <s>uromaṇḍala</s> are used.
One should make <s>karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> in <s>Vaiśākharecita</s>.

children.text: ādyaṃ tu janitaṃ kṛtvā pādamekaṃ prasārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having first performed <s>janita</s>, one should extend one foot.
Likewise one should make <s>alātaka</s> and turn the <s>trika</s> (lower torso).
One should make the left hand <s>añcita</s> and press it at the region of the cheek.
And likewise one should employ <s>kaṭicchinna</s> in <s>Parāvṛtta</s>.

children.text: svastikaṃ karaṇaṃ kṛtvā vyaṃsitau ca karau punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the <s>svastika</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, and again the two hands in <s>vyaṃsita</s>,
One should employ <s>alātaka</s>, <s>ūrdhvajānu</s>, and <s>nikuñcita</s>,
and also <s>ardhasūcī</s> and <s>vikṣipta</s> in <s>udvṛttākṣiptaka</s>.
In the <s>aṅgahāra</s> called <s>Alātaka</s>, there are <s>karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s>;
having bent the hands at the chest, one should employ <s>ūrdhvajānu</s>.
Having made <s>ākṣiptasvastika</s>, one should turn the <s>trika</s> (lower torso);
the hands are in <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>, and there are <s>nitamba</s> and <s>karihastaka</s>;
and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> too is prescribed in <s>pārśvaccheda</s>.
One should set the left foot as <s>sūcī</s> and the right as <s>vidyudbhrānta</s>;

children.text: dakṣiṇena punaḥ sūcī vidyudbhrāntaṃ ca vāmataḥ
children.translated_text: then with the right there is <s>sūcī</s>, and <s>vidyudbhrānta</s> on the left.

children.text: paricchinnaṃ tathā caiva hyatikrāntaṃ ca vāmakam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise there is <s>paricchinna</s>, and <s>atikrānta</s> with the left foot;
with <s>kaṭicchinna</s>, called <s>latā</s>, this is remembered as <s>Vidyudbhrānta</s>.
Having made the foot <s>nūpura</s>, with the right and left hands hanging down,
the hands at the sides, one should then employ <s>vikṣipta</s> with them.

children.text: tābhyāṃ sūcī tathā caiva trikaṃ tu parivartayet ||
children.translated_text: With those two one should likewise perform <s>sūcī</s>, and turn the <s>trika</s> (lower torso).
In <s>udvṛttaka</s> one should always perform the movement called <s>latā</s>, together with <s>kaṭicchinna</s>.
With the hands in <s>ālīḍha</s> and <s>vyaṃsita</s>, one should strike them at the shoulder-tips.
The left foot is <s>nūpura</s>, and the right is <s>alāta</s>;
with that very arrangement one should do <s>ākṣiptaka</s>, while the hands are in <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>.
One should employ <s>karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> in <s>ālīḍha</s>.

children.text: hastaṃ tu recitaṃ kṛtvā pārśvamānasya recayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the hand <s>recita</s>, one should make the side of the body <s>recita</s>;
again, by that same combination, one should make the body itself <s>recita</s>.
The <s>recita</s> <s>karaṇa</s> is to be performed, and <s>uromaṇḍala</s> as well;
and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> should be performed in the <s>aṅgahāra</s> called <s>Recita</s>.

children.text: nūpuraṃ caraṇaṃ kṛtvā trikaṃ tu parivartayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the foot <s>nūpura</s>, one should turn the <s>trika</s> (lower torso);
with the hand in <s>vyaṃsita</s>, one should turn the <s>trika</s> itself.
Having made <s>alātaka</s> on the left, one should join <s>sūcī</s> right there.
One should always perform <s>karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> in <s>ācchurita</s>.

children.text: recitau svastikau pādau recitau svastikau karau ||
children.translated_text: The feet are crossed and <s>recita</s>; the hands are crossed and <s>recita</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā viśleṣamevaṃ tu tenaiva vidhinā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus made the separation, then again by that same rule,
one should cause the re-raising too to be done with <s>recita</s> movements alone.
In <s>udvṛttākṣiptaka</s> as well there is <s>uromaṇḍala</s>,

children.text: nitambaṃ karihastaṃ ca kaṭicchinnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: with <s>nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>kaṭicchinna</s>.
This is remembered as the rule of the <s>karaṇas</s> for <s>ākṣiptarecita</s>.
Having performed the <s>vikṣipta</s> <s>karaṇa</s>, with the hand and foot coming forward,
one should cast out the left hand together with the left <s>sūcī</s>.
The right hand should be at the chest-position, and the <s>trika</s> (lower torso) should be turned.
In <s>nūpurākṣiptaka</s> as well, and also in <s>ardhasvastika</s>,
there are <s>nitamba</s>, <s>karihasta</s>, and likewise <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>;
and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> should be performed in <s>sambhrānta</s> by those who apply <s>nṛtta</s> (pure dance).
Having made the <s>apakrānta</s> step and the <s>vyaṃsita</s> hand,
one should perform <s>udveṣṭita</s> and likewise <s>ardhasūcī</s>;
also <s>vikṣipta</s> together with <s>kaṭicchinna</s>, and similarly <s>udvṛttākṣiptaka</s>.
<s>Karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> should be performed in <s>apasarpita</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā nūpurapādaṃ ca drutamākṣipya ca kramam ||
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>nūpura</s> foot and quickly thrown out the step,

children.text: pādasya cānugau hastau trikaṃ ca parivartayet
children.translated_text: with the hands following the foot, one should turn the <s>trika</s> (lower torso).
Having bent the hand and foot, then again there is <s>uromaṇḍalaka</s>;
<s>karihasta</s> and <s>kaṭicchinna</s> should be done in <s>ardhanikuṭṭaka</s>.
These thirty-two <s>aṅgahāras</s> have been fully stated, O best of twice-born sages.
Now listen to me as I describe the four <s>recakas</s>.
The first is <s>pādarecaka</s>; the second is <s>kaṭirecaka</s>.
The third is <s>kararecaka</s>, and the fourth is <s>kaṇṭharecaka</s>.
Seeing <s>Śaṅkara</s> dancing with <s>recakas</s> and <s>aṅgahāras</s>,
and <s>Pārvatī</s> too dancing with a delicate mode of performance,
with <s>mṛdaṅga</s>s, <s>bherī</s>s, <s>paṭaha</s>s, <s>bhāṇḍa</s>s, <s>ḍiṇḍima</s>s, and <s>gomukha</s>s,
with <s>paṇava</s>s and <s>dadura</s>s, and with all instruments being played,
at twilight, when <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice had been destroyed, <s>Maheśvara</s>
danced with many <s>aṅgahāras</s> that followed rhythm and measure.
Then, seeing the <s>piṇḍībandhas</s>, the <s>gaṇas</s> headed by <s>Nandibhadra</s>
gave names to those <s>piṇḍīs</s> and established their formation together with their defining marks.
For <s>Īśvara</s> the <s>piṇḍī</s> is <s>Īśvarī</s>, and for <s>Nandin</s> it is <s>Paṭṭasī</s>.
For <s>Caṇḍikā</s> the <s>piṇḍī</s> is indeed <s>Siṃhavāhinī</s>.
For <s>Viṣṇu</s> there is <s>Tārkṣyapiṇḍī</s>; for <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, <s>Padmapiṇḍī</s>.
For <s>Śakra</s> the <s>piṇḍī</s> is <s>Airāvatī</s>, while the fish <s>piṇḍī</s> is <s>Mānmathī</s>.
The peacock <s>piṇḍī</s> belongs to <s>Kumāra</s>; the form <s>piṇḍī</s> belongs to <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: dhārāpiṇḍī ca jāhnavyāḥ pāśapiṇḍī yamasya ca
children.translated_text: The stream <s>piṇḍī</s> belongs to <s>Jāhnavī</s>, and the noose <s>piṇḍī</s> to <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: vāruṇī ca nadīpiṇḍī yākṣī syāddhanadasya tu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāruṇī</s> is the river <s>piṇḍī</s>, while the <s>Yākṣī</s> belongs to <s>Dhanada</s>.
The plough <s>piṇḍī</s> belongs to <s>Bala</s>, and the serpent <s>piṇḍī</s> to the serpent-beings.
<s>Gāṇeśvarī</s> is the great <s>piṇḍī</s>, the crusher of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice;
<s>Raudrī</s>, set in the shape of a trident, belongs to the enemy of <s>Andhaka</s>.
Thus also, for the other deities, in due order,
well-marked <s>piṇḍībandhas</s>, serving as their emblems, are to be employed.
The <s>recakas</s>, the <s>aṅgahāras</s>, and likewise the <s>piṇḍībandhas</s>,
after being created by the Blessed Lord, were then given to the sage <s>Taṇḍu</s> for the <s>tāṇḍava</s>.
By him too, afterward, properly accompanied by song and instruments,

children.text: nṛttaprayogaḥ sṛṣṭo yaḥ sa tāṇḍava iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: the performance of <s>nṛtta</s> (pure dance) that was created is remembered as <s>tāṇḍava</s>.
The sages said:
When, for the attainment of meanings, <s>abhinaya</s> (dramatic expression) is performed by those who know it,
Why indeed was this <s>nṛtta</s> made, and what natural basis does it depend on?
It is not connected with the meaning of the song, nor is it expressive of the meaning.
Why then was this <s>nṛtta</s> made for songs and for <s>āsārita</s>s?
<s>Bharata</s>:
On this point it is said: <s>nṛtta</s> does not in fact depend on any meaning at all.

children.text: kiṃ tu śobhāṃ prajanayediti nṛttaṃ pravartitam
children.translated_text: Rather, <s>nṛtta</s> was instituted with the thought that it would produce beauty.
For the most part, <s>nṛtta</s> is naturally pleasing to all people.
And, because it is auspicious, this <s>nṛtta</s> has been proclaimed.
At weddings, births, receptions, rejoicings, prosperity rites, and the like,
and because it is a cause of amusement, this <s>nṛtta</s> was instituted.
And for that very reason, for warding off hosts of spirits, they were set in motion:
the proper divisions of <s>nṛtta</s> that are employed at the beginning of songs.
And <s>Taṇḍu</s> too was instructed by the god: 'With <s>tāṇḍava</s> as the preliminary,
let this <s>nṛtta</s> be set in motion, relying on the performance of song.'
For the rule of <s>tāṇḍava</s> generally has praise of the gods as its basis,
while the delicate performance arises from the erotic sentiment.
Of that <s>tāṇḍava</s> employed by <s>Taṇḍu</s>, its procedure and rite,
taking up the <s>vardhamānaka</s>, I shall now declare the defining characteristics.
Because of the increase of the <s>kalā</s>s and the enlargement of the syllables,
and also because of the increase of <s>laya</s> (tempo), it is called <s>vardhamānaka</s>.
Having arranged the <s>kutapa</s> (orchestra) properly, O best of twice-borns,
the performers should then carry out the <s>āsārita</s> performance.
There, after performing the <s>upohana</s> (prelude), accompanied by string-song,
the dancer's entrance should be made, accompanied by instrumental music.
In a <s>jāti</s> with pure <s>karaṇa</s>s, the music should be applied,
and, with movement following the instruments, her <s>cārī</s> should be employed.
Standing here in the <s>Vaiśākha</s> posture, moving with all the <s>recaka</s>s,
and holding a flower-offering, she should enter the stage pavilion.
After releasing the flower-offering and circling the stage,
and after bowing to the deities, she should then perform <s>abhinaya</s>.

children.text: yatrābhineyaṃ gītaṃ syāttatra vādyaṃ na yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Where the song is to be acted out, instrumental music should not be joined to it.
But in the performance of an <s>aṅgahāra</s>, instrumental music is prescribed.

children.text: samaṃ raktaṃ vibhaktaṃ ca sphuṭaṃ śuddhaprahārajam ||
children.translated_text: In <s>tāṇḍava</s>, musicians should apply music that is even, attractive, well divided, clear, and produced by pure strokes,
music that grasps the limbs of the <s>nṛtta</s>.
After song and instrumental music have been performed, the dancer should then exit.
According to this very procedure, other dancers enter separately.
Then other women, in sequence, who form the <s>piṇḍī</s>,
should perform the <s>Paryastaka</s> until the <s>piṇḍī</s> has been formed.

children.text: piṇḍīṃ baddhvā tataḥ sarvā niṣkrāmeyuḥ striyastu tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After forming the <s>piṇḍī</s>, all those women should then exit.
During the formations of <s>piṇḍī</s>, music should be played here by the instrumentalists.
It should match the measure of the <s>Paryastaka</s> and be furnished with a varied flow of <s>karaṇa</s>s.
There the <s>upavāhana</s> should again be performed just as before.
Then the singing of the <s>āsārita</s> should again be performed.
According to the previous procedure, the dancer should also enter.
She should act out the meaning of the song of the second <s>āsārita</s>,
and that same matter should again be displayed through <s>nṛtta</s> as well.
When the <s>āsārita</s> is completed, the dancer should then exit.
Others enter as before; the performance is the very same.

children.text: evaṃ pade pade kāryo vidhirāsāritasya tu ||
children.translated_text: Thus, step by step, the procedure of the <s>āsārita</s> should be carried out,
both for instrumental performance and likewise for singing.

children.text: ekā tu prathamaṃ yojyā dve dvitīyaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: First one dancer should be employed, then two for the second,

children.text: tisro vastu tṛtīyaṃ tu catasrastu caturthakam
children.translated_text: three for the third <s>vastu</s>, and four for the fourth.
Four procedures for <s>piṇḍī</s>s have been proclaimed:
<s>piṇḍī</s>, <s>śṛṅkhalikā</s>, <s>latābandha</s>, and then <s>bhedyaka</s>.
The <s>piṇḍībandha</s> is so called from compactness; <s>śṛṅkhalikā</s> is a clustered chain.

children.text: jālopanaddhā ca latā sanṛtto bhedyakaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>latā</s> is interlaced like a net, and <s>bhedyaka</s> is remembered as accompanied by dance.

children.text: piṇḍībandhaḥ kaniṣṭhe tu śṛṅkhalā tu layāntare ||
children.translated_text: The <s>piṇḍībandha</s> is in the lowest level, while <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> is in another <s>laya</s> (tempo);

children.text: madhyame ca latābandho jyeṣṭhe caivātha bhedyakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>latābandha</s> is in the middle level, and <s>bhedyaka</s> in the highest.
The various bases of the <s>piṇḍī</s>s are <s>yantra</s> and likewise <s>bhadrāsana</s>,
and also <s>śikṣāyoga</s>; these should be employed by performers.
In this way the performance is to be carried out in the <s>vardhamāna</s>, O ascetics.

children.text: gītānāṃ chandakānāṃ ca bhūyo vakṣyāmyahaṃ vidhim
children.translated_text: I shall further explain the rule for songs and <s>chandaka</s>s.
Of songs, those that are bound to <s>vastu</s> and those that are made into <s>aṅga</s>s,
I shall explain their performance with <s>nṛtta</s> and instrumental music.
There the dancer's entrance should be made with the full instrumental ensemble,
formed with <s>kṣepa</s> and <s>pratikṣepa</s>, and prepared by the instrumental <s>upohana</s>.
First, in the song, every <s>vastu</s> should be acted out,
and that same matter should again be displayed through <s>nṛtta</s> as well.
The procedure that was stated earlier for <s>nṛtta</s>, <s>abhinaya</s>, and instrumental playing,
in the rule for the <s>āsārita</s>, should also apply to the <s>vastu</s>s of songs.
Thus the rule for <s>gītaka</s>s bound to <s>vastu</s> is remembered.
Now listen also to the defining characteristics of songs bound to <s>aṅga</s>s.
The very rule for <s>vastuka</s>s, concerning <s>nṛtta</s>, <s>abhinaya</s>, and instrumental playing,
should also be applied to the <s>chandaka</s>s bound to <s>aṅga</s>s.
One should make the instrumental music with heavy syllables and also with light syllables,
in the opening with <s>upohana</s>, according to the extension of the syllables.
When, because of the song, the <s>aṅga</s> returns again and again,
There the first part should be enacted, and the remainder should be joined with <s>nṛtta</s> (dance),
when, under the control of the song, the section returns again and again.
There the instrumental music should be employed together with the three-beat tempo;
as the tempo is, so the instrumental playing should be done here by the players.
In this way this rule is to be applied also in <s>āsārita</s> songs;
understand this delicate mode, for it rests on praise of the gods.
The dialogue between a woman and a man that arises from desire
is to be known as delicate, since it arises from the <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s> (erotic sentiment).
In whichever situation <s>nṛtta</s> is to be applied by performers,

children.text: tatsarvaṃṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi tacca me śṛṇuta dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain all of that; listen to me, twice-born ones.
At the conclusion of an <s>aṅga</s>-theme, and likewise at the returns of a <s>varṇa</s>,
and also at a point of rising intensity, the expert should employ <s>nṛtta</s>.
Whatever is seen between husband and wife and rests on passion,
<s>nṛtta</s> should be employed there, arising from the quality whose purpose is delight.
Where, when the beloved is present, there is the sight of the season and the like,
<s>nṛtta</s> connected with the meaning of the song is desired there also.
But where a young woman is <s>khaṇḍitā</s>, <s>vipralabdhā</s>, or <s>kalahāntaritā</s>,

children.text: yasminnaṅge tu yuvatirna nṛttaṃ tatra na yojayet ||
children.translated_text: in that <s>aṅga</s> no <s>nṛtta</s> should be applied.
In conversation set in motion by a female friend, and likewise when the beloved is not present,

children.text: na hi nṛttaṃ prayoktavyaṃ yasyā na proṣitaḥ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>nṛtta</s> should not be employed for a woman whose beloved has not gone abroad.
But in the <s>aṅga</s> where the heroine gradually receives appeasement,
from that point onward <s>nṛtta</s> should be applied in the remaining <s>aṅgas</s>.
And if an <s>aṅga</s> is made with divine praise as its basis,
one should perform it with the vigorous <s>aṅgahāras</s> of <s>Maheśvara</s>.
But a song connected with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and resting on woman and man
should be performed with graceful <s>aṅgahāras</s> made for <s>Devī</s>.
For the <s>catuṣpadā</s>, <s>narkuṭaka</s>, <s>khañjaka</s>, and <s>parigītaka</s>,
I shall explain the arrangement concerning the rule for instrumental accompaniment.
When there is a <s>catuṣpadā</s> joined with <s>khañja</s> and <s>narkuṭa</s>,

children.text: pādānte sannipāte tu tasyā bhāṇḍagraho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: at the cadence at the end of a foot there should be the taking up of the instruments.

children.text: yā dhruvā chandasā yaktā samapādā samākṣarā
children.translated_text: For the <s>dhruvā</s> that is joined with meter, with equal feet and equal syllables,

children.text: tasyāḥ pādāvasāne tu pradeśinyā graho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: at the end of its foot there should be the cue with the forefinger.
Having made one turn of the singing and of the acting,
one should again connect the return of the foot with instrumental music.
At the conclusion of an <s>aṅga</s>-theme and at transitions between <s>varṇas</s>,
and also at the presentation, instrumental music should be employed.
Those intermediate passages that are produced by string and voice techniques,

children.text: teṣu sūcī prayoktavyā bhāṇḍena saha tāṇḍave ||
children.translated_text: in them a <s>sūcī</s> should be employed in the <s>tāṇḍava</s>, together with the instruments.
Whoever performs this deed of <s>Maheśvara</s>
goes to <s>Śivaloka</s>, his self purified of all sins.
Thus this rule of the <s>tāṇḍava</s> has been set forth with respect to performance.
What else should now be spoken concerning the rule of the <s>nāṭyaveda</s>?
After hearing the rule of the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s>, the greatest sages again
all said to <s>Bharata</s>: "Tell us the five questions."

children.text: ye rasā iti paṭhyante nāṭye nāṭyavicakṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>rasas</s> that are recited in drama by those skilled in drama:
by what do they have the nature of <s>rasa</s>? You should explain this.

children.text: bhāvāścaiva kathaṃ proktāḥ kiṃ vā te bhāvayantyapi
children.translated_text: And how are the <s>bhāvas</s> stated? What indeed do they bring into being?

children.text: saṃgrahaṃ kārikāṃ caiva niruktaṃ caiva tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Also the <s>saṅgraha</s>, the <s>kārikā</s>, and the <s>nirukta</s>, in their true nature.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā munīnāṃ bharato muniḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of those sages, <s>Bharata</s> the sage
again spoke a statement setting out the <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s>.
I shall tell you, treasures of asceticism, completely,

children.text: saṃgrahaṃ kārikāṃ caiva niruktaṃ ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>saṅgraha</s>, the <s>kārikā</s>, and the <s>nirukta</s>, in due order.
It is not possible in any way to reach the end of this <s>nāṭya</s>,
because knowledges are numerous and the crafts also are endless.

children.text: ekasyāpi na vai śakyastvanto jñānārṇavasya hi
children.translated_text: Indeed, the end cannot be reached even of a single ocean of knowledge;
how much less, then, of other knowledges, with respect to the true nature of their meanings?
But, in a brief aphoristic treatment that makes the meaning ascertainable by inference,
I shall explain the summary of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and the rest for this <s>nāṭya</s>.
Of meanings that have been taught at length in <s>sūtra</s> and commentary,

children.text: nibandho yaḥ samāsena saṅgrahaṃ taṃ vidurbudhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise know as <s>saṅgraha</s> that concise composition.
<s>Rasas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, <s>abhinayas</s>, <s>dharmī</s>, <s>vṛttis</s>, and <s>pravṛttis</s>,
success, notes, instruments, song, and stage: this is the <s>saṅgraha</s>.
The meaning that is stated by the wise in brief, with few words,
is to be inferred from the <s>sūtra</s>; the <s>kārikā</s> shows the meaning.
Arising from many names and bases, accompanied by lexicons and Vedic texts,
joined with causal explanation from the meaning of roots, and established by many doctrines,
where a fixed meaning becomes, in brief, an indicator of the sense,
through the statement of the root-meaning, that here they call <s>nirukta</s>.

children.text: saṅgraho yo mayā proktaḥ samāsena dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>saṅgraha</s> that I have stated briefly, best of twice-born ones,
I shall explain its expansion, together with <s>nirukta</s> and <s>kārikā</s>.
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>Hāsya</s>, <s>Karuṇa</s>, <s>Raudra</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and <s>Bhayānaka</s>,
and the two called <s>Bībhatsa</s> and <s>Adbhuta</s>: these eight are remembered as <s>rasas</s> in <s>nāṭya</s>.

children.text: ete hyaṣṭau rasāḥ proktā druhiṇena mahātmanā
children.translated_text: These eight <s>rasas</s> were taught by the great-souled <s>Druhiṇa</s>;
and now I shall explain the <s>bhāvas</s>, born as enduring, transitory, and psychophysical states.
Love, laughter, sorrow, anger, energy, and fear,
together with disgust and wonder: these are proclaimed as the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s>.
<s>Nirveda</s> (disillusionment), <s>glāni</s> (weariness), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), and <s>śrama</s> (fatigue),

children.text: ālasyaṃ caiva dainyaṃ ca cintāmohaḥ smṛtirdhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>ālasya</s> (indolence), <s>dainya</s> (dejection), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>moha</s> (bewilderment), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), and <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness);

children.text: vrīḍā capalatā harṣa āvego jaḍatā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>capalatā</s> (restlessness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), and likewise <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor),

children.text: garvo viṣāda autsukyaṃ nidrāpasmāra eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>autsukya</s> (eager longing), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>apasmāra</s> (seizure);
<s>supta</s> (sleeping), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>avahittha</s> (concealment), and then <s>ugratā</s> (fierceness),
<s>mati</s> (resolve), <s>vyādhi</s> (illness), then <s>unmāda</s> (madness), and likewise <s>maraṇa</s> (death),
and also <s>trāsa</s> (terror) and <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) are to be known as <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory states).
These thirty-three <s>bhāvas</s> (states) have been stated by name.
<s>Stambha</s> (paralysis), <s>sveda</s> (sweat), then <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation), <s>svarabheda</s> (change of voice), and then <s>vepathu</s> (trembling),
<s>vaivarṇya</s> (change of color), <s>aśru</s> (tears), and <s>pralaya</s> (collapse): these eight are remembered as <s>sāttvika</s> states.
Bodily, verbal, costume-based, and likewise <s>sāttvika</s>,
these four are the <s>abhinayas</s> (modes of acting), to be known as belonging to drama.
The <s>dharmī</s> (mode of representation) is remembered as twofold: <s>lokadharmī</s> and <s>nāṭyadharmī</s>.
<s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Sātvatī</s>, <s>Kaiśikī</s>, and likewise <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>:

children.text: catasro vṛttayo hyetā yāsu nāṭyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: these four <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) are those in which drama is established.
<s>Āvantī</s>, <s>Dākṣiṇātyā</s>, and likewise <s>Auḍhramāgadhī</s>,
and <s>Pāñcālamadhyamā</s>: these are to be known as the <s>pravṛttis</s> (regional usages).

children.text: daivikī mānuṣī caiva siddhiḥ syāddvividhaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Siddhi</s> (success) is indeed twofold: divine and human.
The seven <s>svaras</s> (notes), beginning with <s>ṣaḍja</s>, are bodily and vīṇā-based;
they are <s>niṣāda</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, <s>pañcama</s>, and <s>dhaivata</s>.

children.text: tataṃ caivāvanaddhaṃ ca ghanaṃ suṣirameva ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tata</s>, the <s>avanaddha</s>, the <s>ghana</s>, and the <s>suṣira</s>
are to be known as the fourfold <s>ātodya</s> (musical instrument), furnished with defining characteristics.

children.text: tataṃ tantrīgataṃ jñeyam avanaddhaṃ tu pauṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tata</s> is to be known as string-based, while the <s>avanaddha</s> is drum-based.

children.text: ghanastu tālo vijñeyaḥ suṣiro vaṃśa eva ca
children.translated_text: The <s>ghana</s> is to be known as the cymbal or clapper, and the <s>suṣira</s> as the flute.
There are <s>praveśa</s>, <s>ākṣepa</s>, <s>niṣkrāma</s>, <s>prāsādika</s>, and <s>antara</s>;
song is to be known as fivefold, furnished with the use of <s>dhruvā</s> songs.
The <s>raṅga</s> (stage) is described as square, oblong, and triangular.
Thus this concise meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>, the compendium of drama, has been indicated.
After this I shall explain the arrangement of the <s>sūtra</s>-text.

children.text: tatra rasāneva tāvad ādāvabhivyākhyāsyāmaḥ . na hi rasādṛte kaścidarthaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: There, first of all, we shall explain the <s>rasas</s>. For no purpose proceeds without <s>rasa</s>.
There, <s>rasa</s> is produced from the conjunction of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicāri</s> states.
What is the illustration?
For example:
just as flavor is produced from the combination of various condiments, herbs, and substances, so <s>rasa</s> is produced from the coming together of various <s>bhāvas</s>.
For example:

children.text: guḍādibhirdravyairvyañjanairauṣadhibhiśca ṣāḍavādayo rasā nirvartyante tathā nānābhāvopagatā api sthāyino bhāvā rasatvamāpnuvantīti
children.translated_text: just as flavors such as <s>ṣāḍava</s> are brought about by substances beginning with jaggery, by condiments, and by herbs, so also the <s>sthāyin</s> <s>bhāvas</s>, attended by various <s>bhāvas</s>, attain the condition of <s>rasa</s>.
Here someone says:
What entity is meant by the word <s>rasa</s>?
It is answered:
because it is capable of being savored.
How is <s>rasa</s> savored?

children.text: yathā hi nānāvyañjanasaṃskṛtamannaṃ bhuñjānā rasānāsvādayanti sumanasaḥ puruṣā harṣādīṃścādhigacchanti tathā nānābhāvābhinayavyañjitān vāgaṅgasattopetān sthāyibhāvānāsvādayanti sumanasaḥ prekṣakāḥ harṣādīṃścādhigacchanti
children.translated_text: Just as well-disposed people, while eating food prepared with various condiments, savor flavors and attain joy and the like, so discerning spectators savor the <s>sthāyin</s> <s>bhāvas</s>, manifested by the acting of various <s>bhāvas</s> and furnished with speech, body, and inner spirit, and attain joy and the like.
Therefore they are explained as dramatic <s>rasas</s>.
Here there are two traditional verses:
Just as, through many condiments joined with many ingredients,
people who know food, while eating, savor a meal,
so the wise savor with the mind the <s>sthāyin</s> <s>bhāvas</s> connected with <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhinaya</s>.
Therefore they are remembered as dramatic <s>rasas</s>.
Here someone says:
Is the manifestation of the <s>bhāvas</s> from the <s>rasas</s>, or rather that of the <s>rasas</s> from the <s>bhāvas</s>?
Some hold the view that these arise from mutual connection.
That is not so.
Why?

children.text: dṛśyate hi bhāvebhyo rasānāmabhinirvṛttirna tu rasebhyo bhāvānāmabhinirvṛttiriti
children.translated_text: For the production of <s>rasas</s> from <s>bhāvas</s> is observed, but not the production of <s>bhāvas</s> from <s>rasas</s>.
And there are verses here:
Since, joined with various kinds of acting, they bring these <s>rasas</s> into being,
therefore these are to be known as <s>bhāvas</s> by those who employ drama.
Just as a sauce is made flavorful by many different ingredients,
so <s>bhāvas</s>, together with <s>abhinayas</s>, bring <s>rasas</s> into being.

children.text: na bhāvahīno 'sti raso na bhāvo rasavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no <s>rasa</s> without <s>bhāva</s>, and no <s>bhāva</s> devoid of <s>rasa</s>.
In acting, the accomplishment of the two comes from their mutual causation.
Just as the combination of condiments and herbs brings food to tastiness,
so <s>bhāvas</s> and <s>rasas</s> make one another manifest.
Just as a tree comes from a seed, and as flower and fruit come from a tree,

children.text: tathā mūlaṃ rasāḥ sarve tebhyo bhāvā vyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so all <s>rasas</s> are the root, and from them the <s>bhāvas</s> are established.
Now we shall explain the production, color, deity, and illustrations of these <s>rasas</s>.
The causes of their production are four <s>rasas</s>.
That is:
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>raudra</s>, <s>vīra</s>, and <s>bībhatsa</s>.
Here:
From <s>śṛṅgāra</s> arises the <s>hāsya</s> <s>rasa</s>, and from <s>raudra</s> the <s>karuṇa</s> <s>rasa</s>;
from <s>vīra</s> comes the origin of <s>adbhuta</s>, and from <s>bībhatsa</s> that of <s>bhayānaka</s>.
That which is an imitation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> is proclaimed to be <s>hāsya</s>;

children.text: raudrasyaiva ca yatkarma sa dnyeyaḥ karuṇo rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the action belonging to <s>raudra</s> is to be known as the <s>karuṇa</s> <s>rasa</s>.
And the action belonging to <s>vīra</s> is proclaimed to be <s>adbhuta</s>;

children.text: bībhatsadarśanaṃ yacca dnyeyaḥ sa tu bhayānakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever sight of <s>bībhatsa</s> there is is to be known as <s>bhayānaka</s>.
Now the colors:

children.text: śyāmo bhavati śṛṅgāraḥ sito hāsyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is dark; <s>hāsya</s> is proclaimed white.
<s>Karuṇa</s> is dove-colored, and <s>raudra</s> is proclaimed red.
The <s>Vīra</s> should be known as fair-colored, and the <s>Bhayānaka</s> as black.
The <s>Bībhatsa</s> is dark blue in color, and the <s>Adbhuta</s> is remembered as yellow.
Now, the deities:
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> has <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity; <s>Hāsya</s> has the <s>Pramathas</s> as its deities.
<s>Raudra</s> has <s>Rudra</s> as its presiding deity, and <s>Karuṇa</s> has <s>Yama</s> as its deity.
<s>Mahākāla</s> belongs to <s>Bībhatsa</s>, and <s>Kāladeva</s> to <s>Bhayānaka</s>.
<s>Vīra</s> should have great <s>Indra</s> as its deity, and <s>Adbhuta</s> has <s>Brahmā</s> as its deity.
Thus the origins, colors, and deities of these <s>rasas</s> have been explained.
Now we shall explain the definitions and examples of them when joined with <s>anubhāvas</s>, <s>vibhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicāribhāvas</s>.
And we shall bring the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> to the condition of <s>rasa</s>.
There, what is called <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> arises from the enduring state of love.
It has the nature of splendid adornment.

children.text: yatkiñcilloke śuci medhyamujjvalaṃ darśanīyaṃ vā tacchṛṅgāreṇopamīyate
children.translated_text: Whatever in the world is pure, fit, radiant, or beautiful is compared with <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>.
One who is splendidly adorned is therefore said to possess <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.

children.text: yathā ca gotrakulācārotpannānyāptopadeśasiddhāni puṃsāṃ nāmāni bhavanti tathaiveṣāṃ rasānāṃ bhāvānāṃ ca nāṭyāśritānāṃ cārthānāmācārotpannānyoptopadeśasiddhāni nāmāni
children.translated_text: Just as the names of men arise from lineage, family, and custom, and are established by the instruction of reliable people, so too the names of these <s>rasas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, and meanings belonging to drama arise from custom and are established by reliable instruction.
Thus this <s>rasa</s>, <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, is established by custom, since it has the nature of pleasing and splendid adornment.
It has women and men as its cause, and its characters are excellent youths.
It has two bases: union and separation.

There, union arises from <s>vibhāvas</s> such as the season, garlands, unguents, ornaments, beloved persons, objects, fine residences, enjoyments, going to groves, experience, hearing, seeing, sport, playful dalliance, and the like.
Its acting should be applied through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as clever movements of the eyes, raising of the brows, movement of sidelong glances, graceful and sweet movements of the limbs, and speech.
Its <s>vyabhicāribhāvas</s> exclude laziness, fierceness, and disgust.

But that which is produced by separation should be acted through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as despondency, weakness, suspicion, jealousy, fatigue, anxiety, longing, sleep, dreams, waking, illness, madness, intoxication, seizure, stupor, death, and the like.
Here someone says:

children.text: yadyayaṃ ratiprabhavaḥ śṛṅgāraḥ kathamasya karuṇāśrayiṇo bhāvā bhavanti
children.translated_text: If this <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> arises from love, how can it have states that depend on <s>Karuṇa</s>?
To this it is said:
It has already been stated that <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is produced by union and separation.
And by the authors of treatises on amorous life it has been described as having ten conditions.
We shall state these in the section on general acting.
<s>Karuṇa</s>, however, arises from curses, suffering, calamity, loss of beloved persons and wealth, killing, and imprisonment, and it is a state without expectation.
The state arising from longing and anxiety, a state with expectation, is produced by separation.
Thus <s>Karuṇa</s> is one thing, and separation is another.
In this way <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is connected with all the <s>bhāvas</s>.
Moreover:
A man who is furnished with mostly pleasurable things and enjoys seasons, garlands, and the like,
and who is joined with a woman, is designated as <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>.
Moreover, here there are two <s>āryā</s> verses imbued with the meaning of the aphorism:
Through seasons, garlands, ornaments, and the enjoyment of beloved persons, music, and poetry,
and through excursions and amusements in pleasure groves, the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> <s>rasa</s> arises.
Through serenity of the eyes and face, smiles, sweet speech, firmness, and joy,
and through sweet movements of the limbs, its acting should be applied.
Now what is called <s>Hāsya</s> has laughter as its enduring state.
It arises from <s>vibhāvas</s> such as distorted dress and ornaments of others, impudence, fickleness, trickery, improper prattle, seeing deformity, pointing out faults, and the like.
Its acting should be applied through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as trembling of the lips, nose, and cheeks, opening and contraction of the eyes, sweat, redness of the face, and holding the sides.
Its <s>vyabhicāribhāvas</s> include dissimulation, laziness, drowsiness, sleep, dreams, waking, and the like.
This is of two kinds: based in oneself and based in another.
When one laughs oneself, it is based in oneself.

children.text: yadā tu paraṃ hāsayati tadā parasthaḥ
children.translated_text: But when one makes another person laugh, it is based in another.
Here there are two traditional <s>āryā</s> verses:
Through contrary ornaments and through distorted conduct, names, and dress,
and through distorted particular meanings, because one laughs, the <s>rasa</s> is remembered as <s>Hāsya</s>.
Because, by distorted conduct, speech, bodily alterations, and distorted dress,
it makes people laugh, therefore the <s>rasa</s> should be known as <s>Hāsya</s>.
This <s>rasa</s> is seen mostly in the roles of women and low characters.
Its six divisions should be known, and I shall state them again.
They are <s>smita</s>, then <s>hasita</s>, <s>vihasita</s>, <s>upahasita</s>, <s>apahasita</s>, and <s>atihasita</s>.
There are two divisions each for the superior, middling, and inferior character types.
There:
<s>Smita</s> and <s>hasita</s> belong to the superior persons, while <s>vihasita</s> and <s>upahasita</s> belong to the middling ones.
<s>Apahasita</s> and <s>atihasita</s> are to be known as belonging to the inferior persons.
Here are verses:
With cheeks slightly opened and with sidelong glances endowed with elegance,
calm, and with the teeth not visible: this should be the <s>smita</s> of superior persons.
With face and eyes fully opened, and then with cheeks expanded,
and with the teeth slightly visible, that is prescribed as <s>hasita</s>.
Now, for the middling persons:
That which has contracted eyes and cheeks, is accompanied by sound, and is also sweet,
timely and with redness of the face, that indeed should be <s>vihasita</s>.
That which has the nostrils expanded and is observed with a crooked glance,
with body and head bent down, that should be <s>upahasita</s>.
Now, for the inferior persons:
And that laughter which is out of place and likewise has tearful eyes,
with shoulders and head shaking, should be <s>apahasita</s>.
That which is vehement, with tearful eyes, a drawn-out voice, and arrogance,
and with the hands clasping the sides, should be <s>atihasita</s>.
The occasions for laughter that arise from the action in a play
should thus be applied to superior, inferior, and middling characters.
Thus this <s>Hāsya</s> is to be known as arising from oneself and also as arising from another;
the comic <s>rasa</s> is twofold, belongs to three character-types, and has emotions in three states.
Now <s>Karuṇa</s>, the pathetic <s>rasa</s>, arises from the enduring state of grief.
It arises from determinants such as curses, suffering, calamity, separation from beloved persons, loss of prosperity, killing, imprisonment, flight, injury, and contact with misfortune.
Its enactment should be performed through consequent signs such as falling tears, lamentation, drying of the mouth, change of complexion, slackness of the limbs, sighing, and loss of memory.

Its transitory states include despondency, exhaustion, anxiety, longing, agitation, confusion, delusion, fatigue, fear, depression, wretchedness, illness, stupor, madness, seizure, terror, laziness, dying, paralysis, trembling, change of complexion, tears, and alteration of the voice.
On this there are <s>āryā</s> verses:
From seeing a beloved person killed, or from hearing disagreeable speech,
through these special emotional states, the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Karuṇa</s> arises.
The pathetic <s>rasa</s> should be enacted with loud weeping, onsets of bewilderment, laments, and wailings,
and also with bodily exhaustion and blows to the body.

children.text: atha raudro nāma krodhasthāyibhāvātmako rakṣodānavoddhatamanuṣyaprakṛtiḥ saṃgrāmahetukaḥ
children.translated_text: Now <s>Raudra</s>, the furious <s>rasa</s>, consists of the enduring state of anger, has <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and haughty humans as its characters, and has battle as its cause.
It arises from determinants such as anger, provocation, reproach, false speech, injury, harsh words, hostility, and jealousy.
Its actions include beating, tearing, tormenting, cutting, taking up weapons, the fall of weapons, combat, and drawing blood.

Furthermore, its enactment should be performed through consequent signs such as reddened eyes, knitting of the brows, pressing the teeth and lips together, twitching of the cheeks, and clenching of the fingertips.
Its states include freedom from confusion, energy, agitation, indignation, restlessness, fierceness, pride, sweat, trembling, horripilation, and a choked voice.
Here someone asks:
Since it has been said that the furious <s>rasa</s> belongs to <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Dānavas</s>, and the like,
does it not exist for others?
The reply is:
The furious <s>rasa</s> does exist for others too.
But here the principal domain is being taken.
For they are furious by nature.
Why?
They have many arms and many faces, with tawny hair tossed upward and scattered,
with red, rolling eyes, and they have terrifying dark forms.

children.text: yacca kiṃcit samārambhante svabhāvaceṣṭitaṃ vāgaṅgādikaṃ tatsarvaṃ raudramevaiṣām
children.translated_text: Whatever they undertake, or whatever is their natural action in speech, body, and so on, all of it is furious for them.
Even erotic love is generally practiced by them with force.

children.text: teṣāṃ cānukāriṇo ye puruṣās teṣāmapi saṅgrāmasamprahārakṛto raudro raso 'numantavyaḥ
children.translated_text: For those men who imitate them too, the furious <s>rasa</s> produced by battle and violent encounter is to be admitted.
On this there are traditional <s>āryā</s> verses:
From battle, striking, killing, mutilating, cutting, and tearing,
and from the turmoil of combat and the like, the furious <s>rasa</s> is produced.
Through the discharge of various weapons and the cutting off of heads, trunks, and arms,
through these specific matters its enactment should be performed.
Thus the furious <s>rasa</s> has been seen, marked by furious speech and bodily action,
consisting mostly of weapon-strikes and the performance of fierce deeds.
Now <s>Vīra</s>, the heroic <s>rasa</s>, has superior characters and consists of energy.
It arises from determinants such as freedom from confusion, determination, policy, discipline, strength, valor, power, majesty, and influence.
Its enactment should be performed through consequent signs such as steadiness, courage, heroism, generosity, and skill.
Its states include firmness, intelligence, pride, agitation, fierceness, indignation, memory, and horripilation.
Here, at the opening of the analysis of <s>rasa</s>, there are <s>āryā</s> verses:
From energy and determination, from not being despondent, and from absence of amazement and delusion,
and from various specific matters, the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Vīra</s> arises.
With firmness, courage, heroism, pride, energy, valor, and influence,
and with words that issue challenges, the heroic <s>rasa</s> should be properly enacted.
Now <s>Bhayānaka</s>, the fearful <s>rasa</s>, consists of the enduring state of fear.

It arises from determinants such as seeing beings with distorted cries, panic caused by jackals and owls, anxiety, going to empty houses or forests, and seeing, hearing, or being told of the killing or imprisonment of one's own people.
Its enactment should be performed through consequent signs such as trembling hands and feet, restless eyes, horripilation, facial discoloration, and alteration of the voice.

Its states include paralysis, sweat, a choked voice, horripilation, trembling, alteration of the voice, change of complexion, suspicion, delusion, wretchedness, agitation, restlessness, stupor, terror, seizure, and death.
On this there are <s>āryā</s> verses:
From seeing beings with distorted cries, and from going to battle, a forest, or an empty house,
and from an offense against a teacher or a king, the artificial fearful state should be known.
Fear is shown by changes in the body, face, and gaze, by stiffness of the thighs, looking around, and agitation,
by a fallen face, drying of the mouth, beating of the heart, and hair standing on end.
This should be natural, arising from inner disposition, and it should be performed in just that way.
Again, the artificial kind should be produced by these very states, but with gentle actions.
With trembling of the hands and feet, paralysis, and quivering of the body and heart...
The <s>Bhayānaka</s> should always be enacted with lips, palate, and throat dried up.
Now the <s>Bībhatsa</s>, so called, has disgust as its enduring <s>bhāva</s>.
It arises from <s>vibhāvas</s> such as hearing, seeing, or mentioning what is disagreeable, unpleasant, repulsive, and unwished for.
Its enactment should be applied through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as contracting the whole body, distorting the face, scratching, spitting, and showing revulsion.
Its <s>bhāvas</s> are seizure, agitation, sudden impulse, bewilderment, sickness, death, and the like.
Here there are two <s>āryā</s> verses in the traditional appendix.
Through the sight of what is unwelcome, and through defects of smell, taste, touch, and sound,
and through many things that cause revulsion, the <s>Bībhatsa-rasa</s> arises.
With distortion of the face and eyes, covering of the nose, and the face bent downward,
and with indistinct falls of the feet, <s>Bībhatsa</s> should be properly enacted.
Now the <s>Adbhuta</s>, so called, has wonder as its enduring <s>bhāva</s>.
It arises from <s>vibhāvas</s> such as seeing divine beings, obtaining a desired wish, going to gardens, temples, and the like, and the occurrence of assemblies, aerial palaces, magic, and conjuring.

Its enactment should be applied through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as widening the eyes, gazing without blinking, horripilation, tears, sweat, joy, cries of approval, streams of gifts, exclamations of wonder, and whirling of the arms, face, garment, and fingers.
Its <s>bhāvas</s> are stupefaction, tears, sweat, a choked voice, horripilation, agitation, excitement, dullness, fainting, and the like.
Here there are two <s>āryā</s> verses in the traditional appendix.

children.text: yattvātiśayārthayuktaṃ vākyaṃ śilpaṃ ca karmarūpaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Whatever statement, craft, or action-form is endowed with an extraordinary meaning,
all that should be understood as taking the form of a <s>vibhāva</s> in the <s>Adbhuta-rasa</s>.
Its enactment is by touches, graspings, excited movements, exclamations of wonder, and cries of approval,
and by trembling, faltering speech, sweat, and the like.
One should know <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> as threefold, consisting of speech, costume, and action.
And <s>Hāsya</s> and <s>Raudra</s> are remembered as threefold through body, costume, and speech.
Born from injury to <s>dharma</s>, and likewise arising from loss of wealth or purpose,
and also caused by grief: <s>Karuṇa</s> is remembered as threefold.
The heroic in giving, the heroic in <s>dharma</s>, and likewise the heroic in battle:

children.text: rasaṃ vīramapi prāha brahmā trividhameva hi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> declared the <s>Vīra-rasa</s> too to be exactly threefold.
From stratagem, from offense, and also from being terrified,
again one should know <s>Bhayānaka</s> to be exactly threefold.

children.text: bībhatsaḥ kṣobhajaḥ śuddha udvegī syāt dvitīyakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bībhatsa</s> is the pure shock-born kind; the agitating kind is the second.
The agitating kind comes from excrement and worms; the shock-born kind comes from blood and the like.
The <s>Adbhuta-rasa</s> is known as twofold: divine and born of joy.
The divine is born from seeing divine things; that born of joy is remembered as arising from delight.
Now the <s>Śānta</s>, so called, has calm as its enduring <s>bhāva</s> and sets one moving toward liberation.
It arises from <s>vibhāvas</s> such as knowledge of reality, dispassion, and purity of disposition.
Its enactment should be applied through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, spirituality, meditation, concentration, worship, compassion for all beings, and assuming sacred marks.
Its transitory <s>bhāvas</s> are disenchantment, recollection, firmness, purity in all life-stages, stupefaction, horripilation, and the like.
Here there are <s>āryā</s> verses and <s>ślokas</s>.
It arises from liberation and spirituality, and is joined with causes whose aim is knowledge of reality;
taught as leading to the highest good, the rasa called <s>Śānta</s> comes into being.
Endowed with restraint of intellect, sense faculties, and action faculties, and with abiding in the inner self,
and concerned with the happiness and welfare of all living beings, it should be known as the <s>Śānta-rasa</s>.

children.text: na yatra duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ na dveṣo nāpi matsaraḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is neither pain nor pleasure, neither hatred nor envy,

children.text: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu sa śāntaḥ prathito rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there is equanimity toward all beings, that rasa is renowned as <s>Śānta</s>.
The <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with love are modifications; <s>Śānta</s>, however, is considered the natural ground.
A modification born from its natural ground dissolves back into that very ground.
Having obtained its own particular cause, each <s>bhāva</s> proceeds from <s>Śānta</s>.
And when the cause disappears, it dissolves again into <s>Śānta</s> alone.
Thus the nine <s>rasas</s> have been seen by those skilled in drama, endowed with their defining marks.
Thus these eight <s>rasas</s> should be known, marked by their characteristics;
from here onward I shall also explain the defining marks of the <s>bhāvas</s>.
Thus ends the sixth chapter, the chapter on <s>rasa</s>, in <s>Bharata</s>'s <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>.
